Cat-Astrophy: How a Build Can Change Every Expedition
items.content:
Summary
How every expedition can lead to a different build.
Change the way you fight through module synergies and directional attacks.
Every build creates a unique path to uncover Polo’s story.
When I enter a new expedition in Cat-Astrophy, I don’t start with a fixed build that I have to repeat. I start with a question: what kind of Polo am I going to build this time? That idea is at the core of the module system, and it’s why two runs can take me down completely different paths, even when I return to a planet I already know.
During each run, I find modules that can modify specific abilities, stats, or systems. Some improve close-range combat, while others favour mobility, defence, or a more strategic approach. The key is that I don’t have to decide everything before I start: the build takes shape through what I find, what I keep, and how I react to each situation.
The most interesting part comes when modules stop working as isolated pieces. Some can evolve, while others hide synergies that only become apparent when combined. An upgrade that seems simple on its own can end up changing the way I move, attack, or navigate a room. At that point, the expedition becomes more than a succession of fights. It becomes an experiment: I try a combination, see what it does, and decide whether it’s worth building around.
The same principle extends to combat. Cat-Astrophy uses directional attacks that can be customized for forward, upward, and downward strikes. Each direction has different variants and can create synergies with my modules. On top of that, fatigue builds up as you chain attacks together, so maintaining a combo isn’t simply about using the same attack over and over. You have to decide when to keep pushing and when to stop and regain control of the situation. The result is a system that rewards precision and adaptation rather than relying on a single optimal combination.
Route selection is also part of the build. Each planet has different mechanics, enemies, and rewards, and you can choose their order from the ship that serves as your central hub. One route might favour an offensive build, while another could work better with a setup focused on survival or mobility. At the same time, rooms don’t follow a single path: you can encounter combat, parkour sections, events, shops, and minibosses, and decide how far you want to deviate from your route to look for a reward.
And even when an expedition ends with Polo’s death, not everything resets. The Star Fragments you collect can be used to unlock permanent upgrades, new options, and new routes for future runs. You can also discover memory fragments that gradually reveal Polo’s past and the truth behind his abduction. This gives every attempt two layers of progression: the build you’re creating now and the possibilities you’re unlocking for later.
That’s why there is no single “correct” build in Cat-Astrophy. You can prioritise fast attacks and combos, look for a more durable setup, or focus on mobility. Even the same planet can feel different when you arrive with a different combination of modules, a different route, and a different approach to combat. The reward isn’t just finding a powerful upgrade, but understanding why it works and what other decisions it can unlock.
For me, that experimentation is the true heart of the experience. Every run starts with a handful of tools and ends up telling a small story through its decisions: the unexpected combination that worked, the risk that paid off, the module that completely changed a strategy, or the route that opened up a new opportunity. In a roguelite, repetition can be part of the challenge; in Cat-Astrophy, every repetition also gives you a reason to try something different.
Cat-Astrophy is out now on XBOX, alongside Steam, Nintendo Switch, and PlayStation. The combination of builds, routes, and permanent progression is designed so that every expedition can start in a similar way and end up completely differently.

Cat-Astrophy is a fast-paced, challenging space action roguelite: its Star Cursor system and evolving modules force you to adapt your build and playstyle in every run, generating chaotic combat and precise jumps. The game delivers constant tension and rewards both improvisation and technical mastery.
In each run, you’ll travel across procedurally generated planets, combining abilities, choosing paths, and mastering parkour and real-time combat mechanics. Runs are unique: find modules that alter your capabilities, discover hidden synergies, and decide whether to take risks or secure permanent upgrades with star fragments. Death is permanent: dying means learning, reconfiguring, and retrying with new strategies.
● Cosmic Procedural Exploration: Traverse different planets each run, with rooms, routes, and secrets that constantly change, forcing you to adapt your decisions on the fly.
● Agile, Strategic Combat: Use the Star Cursor to direct precise attacks while moving Polo; action is fluid, sharp, and packed with risk-reward moments.
● Unique Builds Every Run: Discover modules and reconfigure abilities to create combinations that completely transform your playstyle.
● Permanent Progression: Collect star fragments to unlock lasting upgrades that open new routes and tactical options between runs.
● Impactful Paths and Decisions: Choose which planets to explore and which rewards to pursue; your choices shape the pace and difficulty of the adventure.
● Parkour and Precision: Deadly jumps and challenging platforming sections that blend movement and combat in every encounter.
● Cosmic Pixel Art Aesthetic: Vibrant worlds, alien creatures, and environments with personality reinforce the game’s tense and frantic tone.
● Mystery-Driven Story: Discover why Polo was abducted and what forces caused the cat-astrophe; the narrative complements the action without overshadowing gameplay.
Cat-Astrophy is for players seeking intensity, replayability, and meaningful decisions. Every death teaches you something new: learn, adjust your build, and overcome what once defeated you.

items.title: EA restores seven classic PC games using recovered archive footage
items.content:
EA has restored seven classic PC games, including Road Rash and multiple Wing Commander titles, after uncovering an archive of long-lost master footage. The newly released Anniversary Editions arrive alongside a wider rollout of classic EA games on Steam, GOG and the EA App.
According to EA, the restoration project began after the discovery of an archive containing thousands of Betacam, VHS and D1 tapes. The footage allowed the team to recover and digitise higher-quality source material, resulting in more than 1,500 restored FMV sequences across the seven Anniversary Edition releases. Alongside the restored video content, the games also include controller support, quality-of-life improvements and other modern compatibility updates.
EA also worked directly with long-standing Wing Commander community modders during development, with some existing fan-made improvements making their way into the official releases. Players who already own digital copies of the affected Wing Commander titles through GOG or the EA App will receive the Anniversary Edition upgrades free of charge on their existing platform.
Alongside the Anniversary Editions, EA has expanded its classic game catalogue on Steam with titles from the Ultima and Crusader series, as well as Theme Hospital, Strike Commander and additional Wing Commander releases. Anniversary Editions are priced at £8.99/$9.99/€9.99, while the remaining classic titles cost £4.99/$4.99/€4.99. Introductory discounts are available on Steam and GOG until 19th November.

items.title: Hozy brings calm, tactile home restoration to PS5 on November 9
items.content:
Imagine actually enjoying cleaning your house or ripping out old tiles. Unhinged, isn’t it?
You put on your favourite music and open the windows to let the fresh air in. The dust disappears, the floor begins to shine with every sweep of the mop, and the rooms start to transform into cozy, welcoming spaces. There’s something incredibly satisfying about seeing it all come together, one step at a time.
That’s exactly what we wanted to capture in Hozy – a cozy, tactile and stress-free home restoration game that is coming to PlayStation 5 on November 9.
Welcome to Littleville
Hozy is a game where you can completely unwind. There are no timers, no scores and no pressure.
Each level in Hozy features a space with its own atmosphere and story. Your first job is to tidy it up and renovate it. Then furnish it using the sets of furniture and décor provided. Don’t worry about being overwhelmed with an endless catalogue – each level features a carefully curated set of items you’ll need so that the end result always looks worthy of the interior design magazine.
Comfort in every detail
To help you tackle the tasks of refurbishing the rooms with ease, you’ll have access to an array of tools: from a simple mop to a crowbar. We all know what it’s like to mop the floors… But in Hozy, even this is a real pleasure. We’ve done our best to ensure that using each tool brings nothing but joy.
You can also interact with the surroundings and a whole host of furniture. Open the window to let the breeze play with the dust particles. Light a lamp by the sofa to create a cosy reading nook. Play a tune on the piano or find secret messages in one of the drawers – experiment with different objects to discover what other interesting effects await you.
Every surface, every object and instrument has its own unique sound. And the music changes dynamically as you progress through the level – we recommend playing with headphones or a home cinema system to fully appreciate the sounds of the world around you.
Immersive cozy gameplay
This is something we’re particularly proud of. When we first started developing Hozy, our main aim was to make using the instruments as enjoyable and responsive as possible. And the DualSense wireless controller is simply perfect for complementing and enhancing that experience.
Thanks to haptic feedback, interacting with objects and surfaces becomes even more realistic, as every action you take is accompanied by a unique set of vibrations. For example, when a mop glides smoothly across the floor or when you’re arranging furniture. Combined with the adaptive triggers, you’ll naturally feel the resistance of the floorboards as they finally give way to the crowbar.
The DualSense’s built-in speaker helps you immerse yourself even further in the game’s atmosphere, subtly emitting additional sounds from the instruments you are currently using.
More ways to play
Once you’ve completed the Hozy storyline, comprising nine unique levels, your journey into the world of cosiness isn’t over yet. Come back to the houses you’ve already restored to discover… new versions of the previous rooms. The ‘Game+’ mode will help you look at these rooms in a new light (literally) – now you can switch between day and night, as well as furnish rooms with different sets of furniture. Some of them will change beyond recognition.
If you fancy creating something truly yours, Hozy has just the thing for you – a Sandbox mode with every item available in the game. Mix and match, duplicate, and customize your rooms however you wish. Who are we to tell you which wallpaper, background colour, window shape, support beams or light switches to choose?
But there’s more: we also have plans for seasonal events and various DLCs, both free and paid.
Make it Hozy
Of course, we haven’t forgotten about the various accessibility features, so that as many renovators as possible can enjoy Hozy. The game is available in 11 different languages and includes a range of visual and control settings. Adjust the movement speed of your tools, invert the camera, change colour display settings and much more.
If you want to make playing Hozy even more comfortable – settle into your favourite armchair, pour yourself a cup of hot chocolate and launch the game on PlayStation Portal.
We’re looking forward to November 9, when you’ll be able to enjoy Hozy at your own pace.

A Blade for the Innocent: Into the War-Torn Hutuo Region of Where Winds Meet on XBOX
items.content:
Summary
Where Winds Meet’s Hutuo anniversary update arrives on XBOX Series X|S on November 13 (PT), bringing a new war-torn campaign centered on the Battle of Zhongdu Bridge.
Players can face new bosses, try Horse Racing Chess and Jianghu Tactics, and wield the Dual Spears martial art.
Anniversary events offer more than $150 worth of gifts, including a free Outfit Set of your choice and 42 Resonating Melody draws and 27 Lingering Melody draws.
As our anniversary theme region, Hutuo, prepares to go live on XBOX Series X|S, we couldn’t be more excited to give you a glimpse of what’s to come. On November 13, wanderers across the XBOX community will step into this active, mud-and-steel warzone, navigating the devastating fallout of a sixteen-year conflict and throwing themselves into the desperate frontline defense at the battle of Zhongdu Bridge.
In Hutuo, the relentless advance of invading northern forces is set to turn the riverbanks into a brutal proving ground. Amid the chaos, we wanted to confront players with the hardest question in Wuxia: what keeps your blade raised when empires crumble and the powers above fail?
Righteousness and Conviction: Rethinking The True Essence of ‘Xia’
In Where Winds Meet, Hutuo delves deeply into the Eastern philosophy of ‘Xia’: a moral compass governed not by blind obedience to authority, but by an individual’s duty to protect the innocent and uphold justice when institutions fracture.
At Zhongdu Bridge, loyalty to a crumbling throne and righteousness toward the people pull in opposite directions. The core of this story is not about glorifying the clash of armies, but honoring the courage of ordinary folk and sworn companions who choose to stand as a living shield before an unstoppable force.
To ground that philosophy, the frontier is filled with intimate side quests showing the war from varied, ground-level perspectives. You will encounter conflicted soldiers choosing conscience over cruel military orders, displaced families holding onto hope along the reed-lined rivers, and nameless villagers risking their lives to shelter refugees. Even in history’s bleakest chapters, true heroism emerges not from imperial mandates, but from the quiet resilience of everyday lives.
Mastering the Frontline: Surviving Hutuo’s Toughest Encounters
Warfare on the frontier demands a more aggressive, tactical approach to combat. If you are preparing to cross the river, mastering enemy stance dynamics is essential.
Conquering the Fierce General, Xiao Han: Serving as the climax of the Hutuo River Campaign, Xiao Han is fortified by Blood-forged Super Armor. To counter his relentless assault, focus on high-impact parries, bait out his overextended thrusts, and execute stance-breaking counterstrikes to shatter his armor before committing to full damage rotations
Taming Moonveil Knoll with Bingshen: This solitary wanderer relies on rapid gap-closers and sweeping area attacks born of lifelong regret. Maintaining spatial discipline and dodging into—rather than away from—his follow-up strikes will give you clean openings to punish his recoveries.
Surviving Yelu Abuli’s Dark Rituals: Facing this mystic royal and shaman requires close arena awareness. Yelu Abuli manipulates ceremonial fire, forcing players to remain mobile, interrupt channeled incantations, and bait area hazards away from the center of the battlefield.
Tactical Versatility: Yuen Woo-ping’s Dual Spears (Arriving Nov 26)
To counter these escalating battlefield threats, legendary action director Yuen Woo-ping (“Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon”) led the motion capture and choreography for the upcoming Dual Spears martial art, arriving November 26.
Designed around fluid transitions, the weapon system combines two complementary combat roles. By executing the Dual-Weapon Skill mid-combo, players seamlessly weave light thrusts (Sustained Firepower) into heavy downward strikes (Stance-Breaking Impact) without resetting attack frames, sustaining uninterrupted offensive pressure against armored targets like Xiao Han.
Two Strategic Tabletop Breaks: Horse Racing Chess & Jianghu Tactics
When you need respite from the siege lines, Hutuo introduces two rich, casual-yet-tactical board game modes playable across the Jianghu:
Horse Racing Chess: Step directly onto the board as living game pieces. Roll dice, trigger familiar Mystic Skills, and race fellow players to the finish line in a lively competitive sprint.
Jianghu Tactics: A deeper strategic mode that brings the game’s Heroic Spirit roster to a tactical board. Victory hinges on clever board positioning, gear allocation, and activating character bonds to build winning synergies round after round.
Optimized for XBOX Series X|S
Exploring Hutuo’s war-torn frontier is built for the XBOX living-room experience, with Smart Delivery, HDR support, AMD FSR 2 upscaling, and an updated interface with larger text. XBOX Series X delivers a 4K upscale from 1080p, while XBOX Series S delivers a 2K upscale from 900p. Memory optimizations help keep gameplay smooth.
XBOX Game Pass Perks
After the update on November 13, simply log in and take part in anniversary events to claim over $150 worth of gifts! Just for logging in, choose a free Outfit Set worth 2,580 Echo Beads, from 12 distinct style, and easily earn 42 Resonating Melody draws and 27 Lingering Melody draws through anniversary events!
To welcome XBOX players to the Jianghu, XBOX Game Pass members could claim a launch Perks bundle featuring 450 Echo Jade, 90,000 Coins, 6 Attunement Stones, 30 Large Tuning Stones, 3 Pillow Pills, and 3 Lingering Melodies. The claim period ended January 7, 2027. There are even more ongoing anniversary perks coming to XGP – stay turn!
Experience a story of unwavering conviction, camaraderie, and the true meaning of heroism, and claim the most generous rewards we’ve offered since launch, available on XBOX Series X|S on November (PT). Come celebrate our first anniversary with us in Hutuo!

Jianghu knows no bounds: Cross-play available on XBOX, PS5, PC, and Mobile. Where Winds Meet is an epic open-world action-adventure RPG rooted in the rich legacy of Wuxia. Set during the turbulent era of tenth-century China, you take on the role of a young sword master, uncovering forgotten truths and the mysteries of your own identity. As the wind stirs across mountains and rivers, so too will your legend rise.
An Era on the Brink. A Hero on the Rise
Explore China's Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms period, where political intrigue, power struggles, and epic battles shape the course of history. From the bustling heart of the imperial capital to the hidden corners of forgotten wilderness, every path is layered with secrets, sights, and stories waiting to be discovered.
Who are you — a hero, or an agent of chaos?
Here, freedom is yours, but every action has its weight. Cause chaos, defy the law, and face bounties, pursuit, even time behind bars. Or walk a nobler path: befriend villagers, forge alliances, and grow your reputation as a hero of the Wuxia world. In a world torn by chaos, become the spark that ignites change and forge your legacy!
An Open World of Infinite Possibilities
From bustling cities to forgotten temples hidden deep within emerald forests, the world flows with life—changing with time, weather, and your actions.
Traverse vast landscapes in Wuxia style: scale rooftops with fluid parkour, ride the windstride across miles in moments, or use fast travel points to leap between regions.
Uncover thousands of points of interests, discover over 20 distinct regions, interact with diverse characters, and engage with numerous authentic activities in a world that teems with life. Explore ancient cities, reveal forbidden tombs, play flutes beneath swaying willows, or drink under lantern-lit skies.
Master Your Way of Wuxia Combat
Build your fighting style to match your rhythm—whether you thrive in the heart of melee, strike from afar, or move unseen in the shadows. Choose how you engage, and build a loadout that supports your playstyle.
Take control of fluid, responsive martial arts combat built around classic wuxia weaponry, skills, and strategy. Wield weapons both familiar and legendary—sword, spear, dual blades, glaive, fan and umbrella. Switch between weapons, bows, and mystic martial arts like Taichi to outmaneuver your enemies.
Create and customize your character and progression, choose your role in a fractured world. Align with powerful factions, explore distinct professions, and forge your identity through your actions.
Adventure Alone or Forge Your Community
Embark on a rich, narrative-driven adventure with over 150 hours of solo gameplay, or open your world to up to 4 friends in seamless co-op.
Build or join a Guild to unlock a wide range of group activities—from intense guild wars to challenging multiplayer dungeons and epic raids.
Prove your might in competitive duels, or step into a shared, ever-evolving world with thousands of fellow adventurers.

Microsoft speeds up Xbox PC app with major performance update
items.content:
Microsoft is rolling out a major update for the Xbox PC app, with the company claiming launch times are now up to 60% faster. The update also refreshes navigation across the app, making it quicker to access games, friends and Xbox Game Pass content.
According to Microsoft, Xbox Insiders will start seeing the improvements immediately. Beyond the faster launch times, Home, Store and Game Pass pages are said to load up to 50% faster, while in-app windows can open up to 65% quicker. Microsoft has also refreshed the library experience with updated filters, improved sorting options and redesigned game cards. Friends, parties and chat features have been moved into the main navigation bar, while search now covers installed games, add-ons and people from a single location.
The update extends beyond the desktop app. Microsoft is expanding its refreshed cloud gaming experience on the web, which was previously available through Insider previews. A new Library tab brings together owned cloud-compatible games and Xbox Game Pass titles, with additional filters for genres and input methods. The web experience is also gaining a dedicated desktop mode for larger screens, alongside new visual customisation options including dark, light and high-contrast themes.
Microsoft says the updated design and navigation elements will also roll out to Xbox cloud gaming apps on supported smart TVs and VR headsets in the coming weeks, bringing a more consistent experience across devices.

After buying EA, Silver Lake and PIF reportedly set sights on Unity
items.content:
Just months after taking Electronic Arts private in a $55 billion deal, a consortium led by Silver Lake Partners and Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund is now reportedly exploring another major gaming acquisition. According to Reuters, the group has recently approached Unity Software regarding a potential takeover.
According to a Reuters report, Silver Lake and PIF have held discussions with Unity in recent weeks regarding a deal that could value the company at around $25 billion. Unity's market capitalisation currently sits closer to $21.5 billion following its latest earnings report. Reuters claims Unity has been working with an investment bank following the approach, although discussions remain ongoing and no deal is guaranteed.
Silver Lake's interest is hardly surprising given that it already owns around 8% of Unity after investing up to $400 million in the company back in 2017. The firm has also become increasingly active in gaming alongside PIF, most recently as part of the consortium that completed the acquisition of Electronic Arts earlier this year.
A deal would take private one of the world's largest game development software companies. Unity's engine and development tools are used across PC, console and mobile game development, and Reuters notes that a successful acquisition would rank among the largest software-sector buyouts in recent years. Unity, Silver Lake and PIF have yet to publicly comment on the reported talks.

items.title: How NVIDIA Open Source Tools Are Helping Researchers Build Next-Generation 6G Networks
items.content:
A year ago, NVIDIA open sourced its Aerial wireless software, joining Sionna and a broader suite of open source tools for accelerating next-generation 6G network development. Together, they give researchers a foundation for testing ideas, comparing results and building on each other’s work — connecting simulation and AI training with experiments on real over-the-air wireless systems.
Today, researchers and developers are using these tools to build 6G-ready networks that do more than just transmit data — receiving signals more effectively, keeping robots and autonomous systems connected when it matters most, and adapting in real time as devices move through the world.
Over the past year, global developer adoption of NVIDIA AI Aerial and NVIDIA Sionna software has grown 10x, while NVIDIA’s open source 5G/6G tools have surpassed 1 million downloads. More than 8,000 research and academic institutions worldwide are using these platforms.
The projects emerging today offer a view of how future networks could look. Each addresses a different challenge, but together point toward a broader ambition for building AI-native 6G networks that deliver connectivity, computing and sensing over a converged software-defined platform for billions of people, machines and agents.
Networks That Help Robots React Faster
A robot picking up an object needs to understand its surroundings and act before they change. When the AI powering that decision runs on a nearby server or in the cloud, the wireless connection becomes part of the response time.
Researchers are exploring a more efficient approach called goal-oriented semantic communications. Instead of sending full images, robots transmit compact descriptions of objects, their positions and their relationships. Transmitting just as much information as needed allows robots to more quickly respond, especially in dynamic environments like workplaces and warehouses.
At King’s College London, researchers connected a camera-equipped robot arm to an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin running NVIDIA Sionna, which supports both software-defined 5G network and edge AI processing. In fruit-packing and cube-stacking experiments with deliberately introduced faults, the approach reduced robot task completion time by up to 52.6% and improved task success compared with sending periodic images.
In addition to quicker responses and less processing overhead, the system also proved more resilient — detecting dropped objects, recovering from unsuccessful actions and, in configurations using a digital twin, checking planned movements for potential collisions before execution.
Networks That Learn to Receive Signals Better
For a firefighter receiving live drone footage or a rescue team searching for a missing person, timely images can help guide urgent decisions. But interference and changing radio conditions can make wireless signals harder to decode, causing errors and retransmissions that delay information from the field.
AI receivers address this challenge by learning to recover information from incoming signals more effectively. Better reception could help responders maintain a clearer, more current view of a fire scene or search area.
SoftBank demonstrated this by integrating a neural receiver into NVIDIA Aerial CUDA-Accelerated RAN (ACAR) and testing it with a commercial 5G smartphone. In controlled tests with interference, the neural receiver delivered higher uplink throughput than a conventional receiver at all 15 tested settings, with a maximum gain of roughly 60%.
Another way to improve reception is to teach receivers about the environments where they operate. Using NVIDIA Aerial Testbed, ETH Zurich researchers found that tuning neural receivers using local measurements reduced block error rates by more than one-third compared with selected pretrained versions.
Networks That Learn When to Save Power
As 6G connects more devices and supports more AI applications, managing energy demand will become increasingly important.
For example, a network may need enough capacity to serve a busy stadium, but demand changes when the crowd leaves. AI can help identify when spare capacity can power down — and when it needs to come back online — so operators can reduce electricity use without dropping connections.
At the University of Leeds, researchers developed a system that predicts network demand 10 minutes ahead and uses those forecasts to guide base station sleep decisions. Before powering down, it checks that neighboring active stations can continue serving affected devices and monitors for changes that require capacity to be restored.
The team tested their approach using a portable, NVIDIA DGX Spark-powered 5G “network-in-a-box” alongside a digital twin for validating decisions against real wireless equipment. The result: researchers reported a 45.6% reduction in RAN power consumption relative to a full-power baseline while maintaining device connectivity.
Networks That Can Be Tested Faster — Before They’re Built
Before deploying a network, researchers need to know how it will perform when hundreds of devices compete for connections or radio signals run into interference. Simulating these conditions helps teams evaluate designs before committing to costly equipment and field trials. But realistic simulations can take hours, limiting how many ideas researchers can explore.
The Centre Tecnològic de Telecomunicacions de Catalunya (CTTC) is accelerating that process by bringing GPU-accelerated radio channel models, running on ACAR, into CTTC’s open source 5G-LENA network simulator. These models calculate how wireless signals travel between antennas and devices — a computation that grows increasingly demanding as simulated networks grow.
In an early evaluation, the approach reduced simulation runtime from approximately three hours to 10-20 minutes, depending on the integration, while preserving the expected statistical behavior and network performance.
Faster simulations let researchers compare more designs, investigate more demanding scenarios and refine ideas sooner. As the industry develops 6G, this could shorten the path from a proposed innovation to a thoroughly evaluated network design — helping teams build better connectivity before deploying it in the real world.
At NVIDIA GTC Washington, D.C., attend 6G Developer Sessions where researchers and developers will showcase more innovations shaping the future of wireless networks.
NVIDIA AI Aerial and NVIDIA Sionna are available on GitHub.

items.title: 20 Years of Gears
items.content:
Summary
Gears of War celebrates 20 years with a special anniversary event in Gears of War: E-Day, honoring two decades of brotherhood, community, and unforgettable memories.
Jump into limited-time Versus and Horde modes, unlock new rewards, claim RAAM as a free multiplayer character.
Get ready for Season 2: Legacy, bringing fan-favorite maps, modes, and character skins back to the battlefield. Season 2 arrives December 1.
It’s hard to believe that 20 years ago, Gears of War launched on XBOX 360 and introduced the world to Marcus Fenix, Dominic Santiago, and the genius of putting a chainsaw on a gun.
Since then, a lot has happened.
We’ve released new games, introduced new characters and enemies, and welcomed millions of players into the world of Gears. But when we think about what makes this franchise special, it’s not just the games or the stories we’ve told. It’s the people who have made Gears of War part of their lives.
Over the years, we’ve heard some incredible stories from our fans. Stories of friendships that started in multiplayer lobbies and have lasted for decades. Of campaign playthroughs with fathers or brothers, or groups of friends who made playing Horde together a weekly tradition. Soldiers that have played during military deployments and couples who met playing Gears, fell in love, and eventually got married. Not bad for a game about chainsawing monsters.
And then there are the stories that hit a little harder. Fans who have shared how Gears helped them through a dark and difficult time, whether it was dealing with loss, feeling isolated, or just needing a few hours with Delta Squad to forget about everything else going on in their lives. Sometimes a familiar game and a few friends on the other end of a headset can make a real difference.
For us at The Coalition, these are the stories that matter most.
We’ve always talked about Gears being a franchise built on brotherhood, loyalty, and having each other’s backs. It’s what makes the relationship between Marcus, Dom and the rest of the Gears so important, and it’s been at the heart of the series since the beginning.
But what’s really special is seeing those same values reflected in the community that’s grown around the games. The friendships, the relationships, the shared experiences, and the sense of belonging that comes from finding your people.
It’s an incredible privilege to steward this franchise, to build on the legacy of the creators at EPIC Games, the voice actors and all the creative collaborators who have had a hand in this universe. And to create games that people care so deeply about.
Thank you for making Gears part of your lives, and for letting us be a small part of yours.
Never Fight Alone.
A Special Birthday Gift
To celebrate our 20th Anniversary, this week we kicked off a 2-week anniversary event in Gears of War: E-Day featuring limited time modes and new rewards. In Versus, play Guardian, where only one leader makes it out alive. And in Horde Siege, try out the For the Queen mode, where the supply cache is disabled, leaving you and the squad to rely on your loadouts.
Tomorrow is the exact date of our anniversary and to celebrate we’re giving away RAAM as a multiplayer character to every Gears of War: E-Day player as a free gift. Just login to claim him instantly.
And beginning December 1, we launch our next Season – titled Legacy – which continues to honor the greatest hits of Gears over 20 years in our maps, modes and multiplayer skins. Season 2 not only brings back some fan favorites from the history of the franchise but lets us reimagine characters in ways we’ve always wanted to see them – like Solemn Memories Dom, whose character skin depicts him in the suit he’s wearing in the famous photo of him and Maria from Gears of War 2.

AI may be the reason GTA 6 reaches PC sooner than expected
items.content:
Recent reports suggest the gap between GTA 6's console and PC releases could be much shorter than previous Rockstar launches. Now, former Rockstar technical director Obbe Vermeij believes advances in AI may give Rockstar another reason to bring the PC version forward.
Speaking to Rock Paper Shotgun, Vermeij speculated that Rockstar could be motivated to shorten the traditional wait between console and PC releases in order to avoid losing sales to AI-generated clones, emulators or unofficial PC versions.
“I think I would be concerned, if I was Rockstar, that somebody would just take the PS5 version and get AI to change it to PC,” Vermeij said. While he acknowledged such efforts would likely be inferior to Rockstar's own work, he believes they could still impact sales.
The comments follow recent claims that GTA 6 could arrive on PC much sooner than expected. Some analysts believe a PC release could follow as early as March 2026, while other estimates place it closer to May. Neither timeline has been confirmed by Rockstar, but both would represent a much shorter delay than PC players have experienced with previous Grand Theft Auto releases.
Rockstar has yet to officially announce GTA 6 for PC and the studio has also remained silent on its plans for the next version of GTA Online. For now, Vermeij's comments offer an interesting theory as to why Rockstar may choose to accelerate its PC release plans, but whether that ultimately happens remains to be seen.

items.title: Nier: Automata’s latest patch somehow requires 366GB of free space
items.content:
Believe it or not, Nier: Automata is still getting new patches a decade later. Unfortunately, the most recent patch for PC did something a little unexpected – ballooning the game's install size to over 365GB.
What should have been a simple 8GB update instead left some Steam users staring at storage requirements normally associated with modern Call of Duty releases. Reports began appearing shortly after the patch went live, with players claiming that updating Nier: Automata now requires more than 365GB of free space to complete the installation process.
Fortunately, Square Enix is already aware of the issue and is investigating a fix. In a statement posted to social media, the company confirmed that it had identified a problem causing the Steam version of the game to display storage requirements that are significantly higher than expected following the latest update.
As a temporary workaround, Square Enix recommends downloading the base game by disabling the DLC through Steam's Properties menu. The publisher says it is currently investigating the cause of the issue and working on a permanent solution. While some recent Steam reviews have called out the storage bug, it appears to be tied to the installation process rather than the game's actual installed size. With a fix already in development, the mishap is unlikely to have any long-term impact beyond temporarily frustrating players who suddenly found themselves needing hundreds of gigabytes of supposedly free storage space.

Razer launches handheld-focused Hammerhead V3 Chroma earbuds
items.content:
Razer has unveiled the Hammerhead V3 Chroma, a new pair of wired USB-C gaming earbuds designed for handheld gaming. Priced at £79.99, the earbuds pair active noise cancellation with dual-driver audio and a 90° USB-C connector aimed at making long sessions on handheld devices more comfortable.
The Hammerhead V3 Chroma support PCs, smartphones and gaming handhelds. Rather than sticking straight out from the side of a device, the angled USB-C connector sits flush against the edge, helping to keep cables out of the way while gaming in landscape mode. The wired design also means there is no battery to charge and none of the latency concerns that can sometimes come with wireless audio.
Inside each earbud is an 11mm dynamic driver paired with a dedicated 6mm tweeter. Feed-Forward ANC helps cut down background noise, while PC players can enable THX Surround Sound 7.1 through Razer Synapse. Audio presets for gaming, music, movies and calls are included, with custom EQ adjustments available for those who prefer to fine-tune their sound profile.
The earbuds carry an IPX4 rating against sweat and splashes, while an in-line controller provides quick access to volume, media and ANC controls. A built-in microphone handles voice chat and calls, and each earbud features customisable Chroma RGB lighting. The Razer Hammerhead V3 Chroma is available now for £79.99/$79.99/€89.99.

items.title: GTA V, Red Dead Redemption 2 and more to leave PlayStation Plus this month
items.content:
Each month, Sony updates its PlayStation Plus Extra line-up with a selection of new and sometimes returning games. On the flipside, the console maker also removes titles from the subscription service on a monthly basis. For November, in anticipation of the industry-shaking Grand Theft Auto VI, Sony is set to remove two of Rockstar’s best-selling games – with GTA V and RDR2 (among others) officially departing PS Plus later this month.
In going to the ‘Last Chance to Play’ section on your PlayStation 5, PS Plus Extra/Premium subscribers will find a list of 11 titles which are set to be removed from the service come the 17th of November:
Red Dead Redemption 2
Grand Theft Auto V
Football Manager 26
The Talos Principle II
Cricket 24
Monster Boy and the Cursed Kingdom
Hotshot Racing
Rock of Ages III
Earth Defense Force 4.1
Rapala Fishing
Yet Another Zombie Defense HD
As mentioned, the two biggest departees are Rockstar’s GTA V and Red Dead Redemption 2. While it is likely that their removals were purposefully made in alignment with the upcoming release of Grand Theft Auto VI on the 19th of November, GTA V in particular has been added and removed from PS Plus multiple times – typically on a 6 month rotation – and so it’s possible that this might have been a coincidence.
Either way, you have a little under 2 weeks to play / complete the above games before they are unfortunately removed from PlayStation Plus.

Nintendo Switch 2 hits new console sales milestone
items.content:
The Switch 2 launched in an interesting time for the industry, with Nintendo’s latest handheld-hybrid arriving at a period of relative instability, owing to external economic factors as well as hardware-related shortages. Despite this, the Switch 2 has managed to continuously grow over its past year and a half on the market – with Nintendo now revealing that the console has eclipsed the OG Xbox’s lifetime sales.
As part of the company’s latest fiscal earnings report, Nintendo updated its public sales data on both the hardware and software front. As of the 30th of September, the Nintendo Switch 2 has officially sold a total of 26.35 million units (an increase of 2.67 million compared to the previous Quarter).
Not only does this mean that the Switch 2 has now hit its first major sales milestone of 25+ million, but the console has also officially surpassed the lifetime sales of Microsoft’s OG Xbox (which ended its run with 24 million units sold).
On the software side, Nintendo also saw a range of its past releases hit (or approach) new sales milestones, with Donkey Kong Bananza selling 5 million copies [5.05M]; Tomodachi Life: Living the Dream nearing 9 million [8.83M] and the evergreen Mario Kart 8 Deluxe – which recently got a Switch 2 update – hitting 72 million [80.46 million when including MK8 on WiiU].
In total, the Switch 2 is currently sitting at an average of just under 3 games per console. Though a far cry from the Switch 1’s ratio of 10 games per system, Nintendo’s latest is still in its relative infancy, and so it will be interesting to see where the console lands once it reaches its 2nd anniversary and beyond.

Each month, all those with an Amazon Prime subscription are privy to a selection of games for free as part of the company’s Prime Gaming / Amazon Luna service. For the penultimate month of 2026, subscribers are able to get their hands on a solid 7 games for free, including Jurassic World Evolution 2; WRC Generations and Squirrel with a Gun.
Being made available via a staggered release, November’s free Prime Gaming titles are the following:
Available now:
WRC Generations (Epic Games Store)
Squirrel with a Gun (Amazon Games App)
12th November:
Jurassic World Evolution 2 (Epic Games Store)
Radiolight (Epic Games Store)
19th November
Werewolf: The Apocalypse – Earthblood (Epic Games Store)
Clem (Epic Games Store)
24th November:
Arcadia Fallen (Amazon Games App)
Whether an intentional move or merely a coincidence, this month’s offerings do not include any games on GOG, with the Epic Games Store now seemingly serving as Amazon’s primary partner for its free game keys. Vera Delivers the Best of Both Worlds: Highest Throughput and Fastest Agents
items.content:
AI agents do more than generate answers. They search for information, query databases, write and test code and take action.
Each of those steps relies on a CPU, with agents moving between GPU reasoning and CPU execution throughout a task.
As businesses put more agents to work, AI factories need CPUs that can execute those steps quickly and support many agents at once, all within the limits of available power.
What this means: AI infrastructure providers need to support more agents without making each one wait longer to get work done. And critically, AI factories are power limited. This means operators need to choose infrastructure that maximizes the work done for every watt.
Why it matters: NVIDIA Vera delivers both fast agent performance and high capacity per watt within a single CPU. That gives providers one CPU for a range of agent workloads, rather than having to mix and match fast and dense x86 parts to balance speed and capacity.
The data that proves it: In a 100-megawatt data center comparison, NVIDIA found that a single Vera CPU performs better than the fastest x86 CPU and the most energy-efficient x86 CPU.
Vera delivers industry-leading agent speed while enabling 1.6x more agents per watt versus the fastest x86 CPU.
Vera delivers 2x faster agent speed with leading energy efficiency compared with the most energy-efficient x86 CPU.
Partners are already putting Vera to work. Early adopters see the same exceptional performance in production-style tests:
Perplexity: Ran agentic coding tasks 1.5x faster with Vera than on traditional CPUs. Perplexity plans to deploy Vera in an upcoming production system.
DeepInfra: Delivered up to 2.2x speed of the best x86 processor on agentic orchestration for its production agent workload, achieving the fastest of the four architectures tested.
ClickHouse: Its standard binary, with no Vera-specific tuning, scaled near-linearly across 176 cores and topped the ClickBench hardware leaderboard.
DuckLabs: Achieved about 1.5x the median TPC-H SF1000 performance of an Intel Xeon 6 baseline.
Daytona: Brought 1,000 agent sandboxes online in 10.8 seconds, and achieved 12.7 completed jobs per second at 2,000 concurrent sandboxes, using Vera versus 88.4 seconds with x86.
Modal: Achieved up to 2x sandbox throughput per core versus comparable x86 hardware, with gains that grow under heavy load.
Learn more about the NVIDIA Vera CPU.

Nintendo isn’t considering another Switch 2 price increase, for now
items.content:
Nintendo says it is not considering any further Switch 2 price increases despite ongoing pressure in the memory market. According to Nintendo president Shuntaro Furukawa, the company has secured sufficient memory supply to continue meeting demand while maintaining the console's current pricing.
According to a Reuters report, Furukawa stated that there has been “no major change” to the wider memory situation, suggesting the supply pressures impacting the technology industry throughout 2026 remain firmly in place. Despite that, Nintendo says it has secured enough memory to maintain both its current pricing and its forecast of selling 16.5 million Switch 2 consoles during the current fiscal year.
The update follows Nintendo's decision to raise Switch 2 prices earlier this year due to rising memory costs. As we reported previously, Nintendo insisted there would be no imminent Switch 2 price hike amid rising RAM costs back in February, only for the company to later raise prices in multiple regions a couple of months later. The increase eventually reached the UK too, with the Switch 2 becoming more expensive in the UK towards the end of the summer.
One key detail Nintendo did not disclose is exactly how much memory supply it has secured. Furukawa did not indicate how long those agreements extend, leaving unanswered questions about what happens once those supplies have been exhausted. For now, Nintendo appears confident that further price increases will not be necessary, but with memory costs still elevated across the wider technology industry, it remains unclear how long that stability can be maintained.
KitGuru says: Do you think Nintendo has finally got ahead of the memory shortage, or is another Switch 2 price increase only a matter of time?

items.title: A Faster, Simpler XBOX Experience Is Coming to PC, Web and Cloud
items.content:
Starting today, XBOX Insiders can try an updated XBOX PC app that launches up to 60% faster and makes it easier to find games, connect with friends, and play.
We’re also bringing the refreshed XBOX web experience to more players and rolling out updates to XBOX cloud gaming apps on supported TVs and VR headsets. These changes are part of our work to make XBOX faster, simpler, and more familiar wherever you play.
We’ve heard where the experience could be better. There’s more to do, and your feedback will continue to shape what comes next.
Here’s what’s changing.
A faster, simpler XBOX PC app
XBOX Insiders will start seeing improvements across the XBOX PC app designed to make everyday actions faster and easier:
A faster, more responsive app: The app now launches up to 60% faster. Pages like Home, Store, and Game Pass load up to 50% faster, and in-app windows open up to 65% faster.*
An easier-to-use Library: Simpler navigation, updated filters, and new ways to organize your games make it easier to browse your collection and find what you want to play.
Friends are easier to reach: Friends and social features are now part of the main navigation, making it easier to see what friends are playing, start a chat, or join a party.
Better search: Search across more of XBOX from one place, with results across games, including installed titles and add-ons, and people, so it’s easier to find what you’re looking for.
A cleaner look and feel: Refreshed game cards, Home, Settings, and animations make the app easier to scan and navigate.
*Performance improvement results are based on our testing and may vary by device, internet connection, system configuration, usage, and other factors.
Bringing the refreshed XBOX web experience to more players
Earlier this year, we invited XBOX Insiders to preview a refreshed way to play through XBOX cloud gaming on the web. Over the next few weeks, we’ll bring it to more players automatically. If you want to try it sooner, head to play.xbox.com.
The updated experience also makes it easier to find and play your games:
Your cloud games in one place: A new Library tab brings together the games you can play through cloud, whether you own them or access them through XBOX Game Pass. Browse, sort, and filter by recently played, genre, input options, and more.
More room to browse on larger screens: Desktop mode makes better use of the space on PCs and larger displays, so you can see more as you browse and find games.
More ways to make it yours: Choose between dark and light modes, along with five new high-contrast options designed to support different visual needs and preferences.
A familiar XBOX experience on more screens
We’re also beginning to bring the refreshed look and navigation to XBOX cloud gaming apps on supported TVs and VR headsets.
Playing on a PC, TV, or VR headset is different, and each experience needs to work well for the screen you’re using. Wherever you play, the basics should feel familiar: finding your games, knowing what you can play, and getting into a game quickly.
These updates are another step toward making XBOX easier to use, more responsive, and more familiar wherever you choose to play. We’ll continue listening to player feedback and improving over time.
How to Get XBOX Insider Support and Share Your Feedback
Thanks to XBOX Insiders for all of the feedback. You can also visit aka.ms/XBOXplayervoice to share what you think.
If you’re an XBOX Insider looking for support, please join our community on the XBOX Insider subreddit. Official XBOX staff, moderators, and fellow XBOX Insiders are there to help. We recommend adding to threads with the same topic before posting a brand new one. This helps us support you the best we can!
If you aren’t part of the XBOX Insider Program yet and want to help create the future of XBOX and get early access to new features, join the Program today by downloading the XBOX Insider Hub for XBOX Series X|S & XBOX One or Windows PC. For more information on the XBOX Insider Program, follow us on X at @XBOXInsider and keep an eye on this blog for all the latest news.
Other resources:
Get the XBOX Insider Hub app
XBOX Insider FAQ
How to provide feedback as an XBOX Insider
For more information: follow us on X at @XboxInsider and this blog for announcements and more. And feel free to interact with the community on the XBOX Insider SubReddit.

items.content:
FiiO has released the Snowsky Mage, a compact USB DAC and headphone amplifier that combines virtual 7.1 surround sound with 60W USB-C passthrough charging for just £22.
Styled like a handheld console, the Snowsky Mage (via Vortez) features virtual 7.1 surround sound powered by a 400MHz SpaceTouch SPV6040D processor. Dedicated FPS, MOBA, RPG and rhythm game presets are built in, while an HRTF-based spatial audio engine handles surround sound processing. The Snowsky Mage also includes separate 3.5mm jacks for headphones, headsets and microphones, alongside AI-assisted noise reduction and a physical microphone mute switch. Dedicated USB-C ports keep audio and charging functions separate, while passthrough charging is available at up to 60W on compatible devices.
FiiO is offering the Snowsky Mage in transparent black, transparent green and grey colour options, all available over at Scan for £22.

items.title: Mahesh Babu invests in Shortgun Games
items.content:
Backing co-founders Jeet Chandan and Vidhit Mehta, Superstar Mahesh Babu joins forces with Shortgun Games. (Photo credit: Press Release)
Actor Mahesh Babu has joined Mumbai-based game development studio Shortgun Games as a strategic investor, backing its ambition to build original Indian gaming franchises for international PC and console markets.
Founded by Jeet Chandan and Vidhit Mehta, Shortgun Games is developing titles exclusively for PC and modern consoles, including PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. The investment amount and Mahesh Babu's stake in the company have not been disclosed.
The studio's flagship project, PROJECT TAKEDOWN, is a narrative-driven action-adventure game being developed for international markets, including North America, Europe and the United Kingdom.
Mahesh Babu said, “India has extraordinary creative potential, and the time is right to build original characters and cinematic worlds from here that resonate across the globe.”
He added, “What drew me to this company is Jeet Chandan and Vidhit Mehta’s clarity of ambition and their drive to create high-end PC and console experiences that stand shoulder-to-shoulder with international studio benchmarks.”
The studio's focus on PC and console platforms marks a deliberate shift from the mobile-led approach that has traditionally dominated India's gaming market. Shortgun Games aims to develop high-fidelity experiences and original intellectual properties that can appeal to global gaming audiences.
To strengthen PROJECT TAKEDOWN's action design, the studio has brought on board Indian action director Vicky Arora, whose credits include Uri: The Surgical Strike, RRR and Tanaav. His team is working on motion-capture choreography, combat pre-visualisation and physical stunt mechanics for the game.
Vidhit Mehta, Co-founder and Director of Shortgun Games, said, “We founded Shortgun Games with a singular focus- to prove that India can engineer world-class interactive entertainment for PC and modern consoles. Having Mahesh Babu sir come on board alongside Jeet and me as a strategic investor is an extraordinary milestone.”
Jeet Chandan, Co-founder and Director, said, “Our goal has always been to build durable, cross-media franchises that transcend regional boundaries. Mahesh Babu sir's trust in our roadmap provides a massive vote of confidence for our entire team.”
The collaboration brings together Indian cinema and game development as Shortgun Games looks to establish original Indian intellectual properties in the global premium gaming market.

items.title: The Wizard of Open Weights: Chris Alexiuk Makes AI Easy With Open Models
items.content:
Chris Alexiuk has a simple rule about open source AI: If you believe in it, be loud about it.
“We should be shouting about this technology from the rooftops,” said Alexiuk, a Toronto-based senior product research engineer in deep learning at NVIDIA who specializes in making open large language models (LLMs) practical for working developers.
Alexiuk’s preferred “rooftop” is YouTube, where he’s built a following teaching curious thousands how to build, fine-tune, evaluate and ship production LLM applications and agents.
“I think the people who will most help us understand how to build and apply AI likely haven’t even heard of it yet,” he said. “Trying to get knowledge and information out to as many people as humanly possible is what continues to drive me.”
Bringing NVIDIA Nemotron to Developers Everywhere
Having spent years teaching developers to build with open models, Alexiuk has concluded that transparency isn’t a feature of good AI; it’s the precondition for it.
“Fully open source AI is necessary for the democratization of intelligence,” he said. “You should have access to the weights, the data that went into it, the training recipes, everything.”
That’s why, on his LinkedIn profile, Alexiuk styles himself “No. 1 Nemotron Fan,” referring to the NVIDIA Nemotron family of open source, multimodal models built for long-running, self-evolving and specialized AI agents.
“I think Nemotron is the most important project that exists,” said Alexiuk, who also uses the pseudonym “Joe Nemotron” across social media. “I’m a firm believer that openness is a very important thing to undertake, so I’m going to be the No. 1 fan of whoever is doing that the best. And that is Nemotron.”
https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/ChrisAlexiuk_captions_9MB.mp4
It’s this matter-of-fact directness and affable approachability that makes Alexiuk’s teaching style so appealing. On the social media platform X, he goes by the handle “llm_wizard.” His avatar: a laughing cartoon caricature sporting a slouchy sorcerer’s hat and brandishing a magic wand.
It’s no surprise, then, that Alexiuk likens Nemotron to a magical library — its users fellow wizards in search of knowledge that can move mountains.
“You’re a wizard in search of prepared spells, and Nemotron has a spell for everything,” he said. “Just choose the one you need.”
In non-wizard terms?
“There’s a category of model that’s going to be close to the kind of work you want to accomplish,” Alexiuk said, explaining that Nemotron supports that whole ecosystem of AI users: from individual developers using a model like Nemotron 3.5 Lightning for repetitive, high-frequency execution work to a company deploying Nemotron Ultra for long-running autonomous agents, deep research and enterprise tasks.
NVIDIAN Chris Alexiuk (left) engages with developers during the Build-a-Claw event at GTC Berlin.
“I think that openness helps more people understand AI and hopefully leads to more people doing really ingenious things with these tools at the limit,” Alexiuk said. “If a tool is amplifying skill, it’s amplifying human expression.”
From Birding to Model-Building
Alexiuk first became fascinated with machine learning in a computational physics class at Trent University in Ontario, Canada.
“After that, I learned about TensorFlow and that you could build image classifiers that ran on your GPU,” he recalled. As an initial one-off project, Alexiuk built a classifier that would alert him whenever his friend’s distinctive pet bird, a Yellow-Faced Gray Budgerigar, appeared in frame on his webcam during shared video game sessions.
“Because we were playing video games, I wasn’t focused on my friend’s webcam, but I didn’t want to miss seeing the bird when it appeared,” Alexiuk said. “And then my whole life changed, because in that instance I realized it’s crazy what you could do with technology.”
Since then, he’s been embedding himself in the open source AI community.
“To imagine within the span of a few years going from freaking out because I could know my friend’s bird was in the camera frame to being able to make any website in a matter of minutes with a model that’s running on my laptop — I cannot wait to see what’s next,” Alexiuk said. “It’s never been more accessible to get into and learn about AI.”
And if another LLM wizard arises to challenge him for the title of No. 1 Nemotron Fan?
“It would be the greatest day of my life to be surpassed by an even bigger fan of Nemotron, who had heard about Nemotron through the work I was doing,” Alexiuk said. “That would be a capstone to my career that I can only dream of.”
Hear more from Alexiuk by following the NVIDIA Nemotron Labs Livestreams series on YouTube.

items.title: More Performance From Every Byte: How Full-Stack Codesign Solves AI’s Memory Challenge
items.content:
Larger models, longer contexts and agentic applications are increasing GPU memory pressure while supply tightens and prices rise — a trend expected to continue through the near term.
NVIDIA works closely with memory partners to rapidly adopt the latest memory technologies. NVIDIA was first to adopt HBM3e and HBM4 technologies into an accelerated computing stack.
But the approach isn’t to simply pack more memory onto the GPU. It’s full-stack codesign. NVIDIA intentionally designs GPUs, CPUs, networking, storage and software together to get more useful work out of memory at every layer of the AI factory.
That matters because an AI factory runs on a memory and storage hierarchy. GPU high-bandwidth memory (HBM) is the fastest, most expensive and most contested tier — with model weights and KV cache competing for limited capacity. Below it sit CPU memory, local SSDs and shared storage, each trading speed for more capacity at a lower cost per bit.
How much useful work a byte does depends on how well the whole hierarchy is used: shrinking what must be stored, placing it on the right tier and bringing it back to the GPU before it’s needed.
Byte for byte, NVIDIA makes the most efficient use of memory at every layer — and the results show it. From NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra to the Vera Rubin platform, HBM capacity per GPU rose roughly 3%, while agentic throughput per dollar rose by up to 30x on SemiAnalysis AgentX.
Agentic Inference Is Putting More Pressure on HBM
Frontier models now have trillions of parameters — the values that hold what an AI model learned in training.
KV cache, which holds the context the model needs to understand each active request without reprocessing the same information, is also expanding. Agentic trajectories carry prior context across repeated model and tool calls, in some cases processing up to 3 million tokens, so each request’s working memory grows over time.
Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) adds relevant enterprise information to prompts, creating even more context to process and retain.
During inference, HBM primarily holds both model parameters and KV cache. The result: greater pressure on HBM.
Why AI Factories Need a Memory Hierarchy
Adding more HBM capacity per GPU is the obvious response to that pressure, but capacity delivers only what bandwidth can move.
Think of HBM as a warehouse and memory bandwidth as its loading docks. A larger warehouse holds more inventory, but the docks set how much can move in and out at a time. Once the docks are at capacity, moving more inventory takes longer and slows response times. If delays exceed the required service level, the added space can’t be used effectively, even as it adds cost and draws power.
That’s also why no operation keeps all its inventory in the closest, fastest space. What’s in motion stays near the line. What’s waiting moves to a larger, cheaper space nearby and returns before it’s needed.
An AI factory faces the same limit.
More HBM can hold more KV cache and support more concurrent users. Every added user shares the same compute and memory bandwidth. But when each user expects fast responses, eventually memory bandwidth is unable to supply data as fast as compute can use it: a limit engineers call the memory wall.
Past that point, extra HBM capacity can’t be put to work, yet it still adds costs and draws power. The data still needs a place to live, but not all of it needs the fastest, most expensive tier. This is why an AI factory manages data across a memory and storage hierarchy.
Maximizing the Value of Every Byte With Full-Stack Codesign
NVIDIA’s full-stack codesign makes every byte of HBM count by relieving pressure from model weights, KV cache and RAG data. It does this with techniques that each target a different source of inefficiency:
Shrink model weights and distribute them across the NVL72 domain.
The NVFP4 format reduces the space required for weights compared to FP8, the lowest precision possible on the NVIDIA Hopper platform. Recent models, including FLUX.2 [klein] from Black Forest Labs, Inkling from Thinking Machines Lab, Beam 1.0 from Reflection, Meta Muse Spark from Meta, Step 5 Preview from StepFun and NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL have been released with NVFP4 checkpoints, demonstrating growing model-builder adoption of 4-bit precision for faster, more memory-efficient inference.
Within an NVL72 system, model weights can be distributed across up to 72 GPUs, so each GPU holds a smaller share of the model — leaving more HBM for KV cache and concurrent users.
Shrink KV-cache and offload inactive context to lower-cost storage tiers.
Applying NVFP4 to the KV cache reduces its footprint compared with FP8, so more context can stay resident in HBM.
NVIDIA Vera CPU helps in two ways. Faster tool execution shortens the time KV cache sits inactive during tool calls, and its large LPDDR memory, connected to NVIDIA Rubin GPUs over NVIDIA NVLink-C2C interconnect, gives paused context a nearby place to wait and return quickly.
When context isn’t actively in use, NVIDIA Dynamo inference software moves it to NVIDIA CMX context memory storage — a tier built for capacity at far lower cost per bit than HBM — and returns it before reuse. Unlike local SSDs, CMX is shared across servers, and unlike enterprise storage, it skips the overhead of long-term data protection that short-lived context doesn’t need. NVIDIA CMX context memory storage partners include Cloudian, DDN, Dell Technologies, Everpure (previously Pure Storage), HPE, IBM, NetApp, VAST and WEKA.
Dynamo’s KV Cache Reuse ties the tiers together, managing KV cache as one system-wide resource across GPU memory, CPU memory and storage, so context computed once can be reused across the system.
Compact RAG embeddings and keeping the index outside HBM.
RAG turns enterprise documents into embeddings — numerical representations that let a system search by meaning rather than keyword — organized into a searchable index. NVIDIA Nemotron Retriever models produce smaller embeddings with higher retrieval accuracy, while the NVIDIA cuVS library enables that index to be built and served across CPU and storage. The knowledge base never occupies HBM, and only the passages the model needs enter context.
The result is less HBM used for model weights, less HBM tied up by idle context and more of it available to serve concurrent users.
More Useful Output per Dollar With Each Generation
Across successive NVIDIA platform generations, tokens per second per dollar has risen far faster than HBM capacity.
On the SemiAnalysis AgentX DeepSeek V4 Pro workload, NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 delivers up to 10x higher throughput per dollar than NVIDIA H200 platform at 100 tokens per second per user, with HBM capacity per GPU roughly doubling. At 125 tokens per second per user, Vera Rubin NVL72 delivers up to 30x higher throughput per dollar than GB300 NVL72, with HBM capacity per GPU up about 3%.
For AI factory operators, the metric that matters is how many useful tokens the factory can deliver within its power budget while meeting user response-time needs. More tokens per second per watt means more work and revenue from the same power, and a lower cost for every token. NVIDIA’s full-stack codesign lowers token costs by increasing the useful work every byte of memory delivers.
Learn more in the video explainer and technical deep dive on how NVIDIA full-stack codesign reduces inference memory pressure.

items.title: Blizzard’s WoW Forever mega-server gamble appears to be paying off
items.content:
World of Warcraft Forever officially launched last night, and Blizzard appears to have pulled off something many players thought would be impossible. Despite introducing a radically different server structure built around mega servers spanning multiple regions, the launch avoided the lengthy queues, login problems and server instability that have often accompanied major Blizzard releases.
Rather than relying on dozens of separate regional realms, WoW Forever consolidates players onto large-scale mega servers capable of supporting far larger populations. This is one of the biggest technical changes Blizzard has made to the Classic formula, leading many players to expect at least some level of launch-day disruption as thousands of users logged in simultaneously.
Instead, the launch has gone remarkably smoothly, a sentiment that has been echoed by fans on Reddit, where hundreds of players have been discussing the stable launch experience. Rather than complaining about server crashes and connection problems, many players have instead found themselves praising Blizzard's ambitious mega-server rollout and expressing surprise at just how smoothly things have gone.
While the launch has broadly been viewed as a success, WoW Classic and Forever developer Josh Greenfield acknowledged that a handful of issues did emerge during the game's opening hours. Blizzard encountered problems with the service managing boats and zeppelins, prompting the team to temporarily add portals while a permanent fix was prepared. Some zones also felt quieter than intended due to layer population settings, another issue Blizzard is actively addressing.
My own experience has largely reflected the wider community sentiment. I was able to get straight into the game without any queues at around 11:30pm last night, with my only issues being one bugged quest that required me to restart the game, and one very annoying crab-fetching quest where the mobs simply weren't spawning in often enough based on the number of players actively trying to farm the same quest item. These were very minor setbacks though, setting me back mere minutes rather than hours. At no point did I have to sit in a queue, which is fantastic for an opening-hour MMO launch.
With the first day now in the books, Blizzard's mega-server gamble appears to be paying off. The true test will come over the next few weeks as player populations spread across the world and more players join the game, but Blizzard has nevertheless delivered one of the smoothest World of Warcraft launches in its history.

Sony provides rare update on PS6 development
items.content:
Sony rarely discusses future PlayStation hardware publicly, but the company has now provided a fresh update on PlayStation 6 development. During its latest earnings call, Sony said progress on its next-generation platform remains on track, while preparations for the company's next console will ramp up from the next fiscal year.
VGC sat in on the earnings call, coming away with some interesting quotes from Sony CFO Lin Tao. During the call, Tao said Sony intends to make “solid progress” on preparations for its next-generation platform, while later adding that development of the company's next PlayStation console is progressing as planned. Sony also confirmed that investment in the new platform will begin from the next fiscal year.
The comments arrived alongside Sony's latest financial results, which showed PS5 sales reaching 97.9 million units after another 2.6 million consoles were sold during the quarter ending 30th September. While hardware sales are naturally slowing as the console matures, Tao said the broader PlayStation platform continues to expand and grow in a stable manner.
Sony also discussed memory procurement during the call, stating that it has already aligned with suppliers on the memory volumes required for next fiscal year. While the company stopped short of explicitly linking those agreements to PlayStation 6 production, the comments came as part of a broader discussion about preparations for future PlayStation hardware.
The wider PlayStation business remains in a healthy position. Sony reported a 9% year-on-year increase in gaming revenue and an 89% increase in operating income, while monthly active users reached a record 127 million during September.

items.title: Hope in the City: Why This Detective Uses a Sketchbook Instead of a Badge
items.content:
Summary
Hope in the City launches November 11, 2026, on XBOX Series X|S, XBOX on PC, and Steam, and will be available day one with XBOX Game Pass.
No traditional detective tools? No problem. Discover how Hope uses her artist’s eye, a sketchbook, and some creative imagination, to solve the mystery of her parents’ disappearance.
Go behind the scenes to discover how we designed a unique investigation system and brought Hope’s sketchbook to life with more than 100 hand-drawn illustrations.
What if your greatest tool for solving the mystery of your parents’ disappearance wasn’t a badge, but a sketchbook?
Launching November 11 on XBOX Series X|S, XBOX on PC, and Steam, and available day one with XBOX Game Pass, Hope in the City is a narrative mystery adventure where you play as Hope Song, a 17-year-old aspiring artist living in Shenyang, Northeast China. Just as she’s preparing to leave for art school overseas, she comes home to find her apartment ransacked and her parents missing.
Hope isn’t a traditional detective. She has no authority to demand answers and people around her aren’t willing to talk. When we began designing the game, we asked ourselves: how would someone like Hope investigate?
The answer was her sketchbook.
Giving Players Freedom to Think
As Hope explores Shenyang, you’ll collect clues, engage in conversations, and discover observations that she records in her notebook. You can combine any two thoughts to see what connections they make. Successful combinations form insights and breakthroughs that unlock new dialogue, locations, and leads. You can also take what you’ve learned to other characters and decide what to ask them.
But this mechanic grew from something more than our love of detective games. We wanted to explore what choice means when the world around you limits your options. Hope can’t always say what she’s thinking or convince others to help. In her notebook, however, she can question anything, make unexpected connections, and consider ideas she would never say out loud.
Her actions may be constrained, but her thoughts are not. That’s where we gave players the greatest freedom.
Notebook breakthrough
Making Every Combination Count
During early prototyping, I noticed something frustrating: whenever players combined unrelated observations, Hope gave the same generic response. After seeing it a few times, it became boring!
So, our writers created individual responses for every combination, even when they don’t advance the investigation. Hope might make a joke, reveal a little of her personality, or stumble toward a subtle hint. We wanted you to feel encouraged to experiment rather than worry about getting things wrong.
Finding the right balance still took extensive playtesting. Some connections we thought were obvious proved surprisingly difficult for players, so we repeatedly refined the notebook interface and clues. The goal was to preserve that satisfying moment when two ideas finally click, while making the “wrong” answers more enjoyable and engaging too.
Gameplay screenshot showing Hope’s notebook and thoughts being combined
Drawing Hope’s World
We also wanted the notebook to feel like something Hope would actually draw, rather than conventional game assets.
Artist Calista Antonio created more than 100 hand-drawn sketches for the game. She approached each page as a quick visual impression, capturing what Hope notices and how she feels, rather than producing polished illustrations.
Given that she’s also a 3D animator, Calista’s process combined 3D tools with drawing. She used the models and assets from the game to block out perspectives and pose characters in 3D, then developed the sketches with linework and digital watercolour. While the game features a sharp angular art style, Calista interpreted
There’s also a little bit of Calista herself in Hope. She also has Chinese heritage and, like Hope, she left Asia at 17 to pursue her passion for art in Canada. Calista drew on that experience to capture the emotions of Hope’s journey. Some of Calista’s own paintings even hang on the walls of Hope’s bedroom, bringing a personal touch to the character and her world.
We’re sharing original sketches and process artwork here for a closer look at how the notebook came to life.
Artist Calista Antonio working on Hope’s in-game sketches
The Mystery Is Yours to Uncover
Hope in the City launches November 11 on XBOX Series X|S, XBOX on PC, and will be available day one with XBOX Game Pass.

Your sketches may be the only clues you have. Play as 17-year-old Hope Song in this narrative mystery set in Shenyang, China. While everyone around her cracks under exam pressure, Hope escapes into her drawings, until her parents disappear. Investigate what happened, connect the clues, and uncover the truth hidden beneath the city's calm.
NO NOTE. NO WARNING.
You come home from school like any other day. But the house is quiet. Your parents are gone, the apartment is in shambles. No note, no warning, no answers.
AN ARTIST'S EYE
Hope isn't a detective. And everyone she turns to seems intent on avoiding trouble. But with an artist's eye, she notices details others overlook, and that's what makes her dangerous to whoever's hiding the truth. Drawing is no longer an escape; it's her best chance to solve her parents' mystery.
Wherever Hope goes and whoever she speaks with, she finds elements that don't add up. Investigate each one and capture your observations as sketches in Hope's notebook. Every detail matters.
FROM OBSERVATION TO TRUTH
Combine Hope's sketches into insights, and keep adding new thoughts until they grow into breakthroughs. Piece by piece, sketch by sketch, watch the picture of what happened to your parents take shape, and grow darker than you ever imagined.
A CITY FULL OF SECRETS
Shenyang isn't just a backdrop, it's a character of its own. Rendered in a bold, stylized art style with an edge, every street, storefront, and shadowed alley is begging to be explored. Wander past neon signs and quiet corners, and let the city's striking visuals pull you deeper into its secrets.
WHO CAN YOU TRUST?
On the surface, it's just home: familiar streets, quiet neighbors, ordinary life. But beneath the quiet, something is hidden. Hope can't be sure who she can trust. And she can't afford to wait for someone to help her find the truth.
Hope in the City is made by the team behind the 2026 GDC Best in Play Winner Sky of Tides and the 2024 Peabody Award-nominated Eternal Spring.
