items.title: The Silver Seas and How We “Ship” New Features for Age of Wonders 4
items.content:
Summary
The Silver Seas, the latest expansion for Age of Wonders 4, is out now and is loaded with pirates, sharks, and more things our players have been asking to see.
Community reactions to the game have helped shape the new things we’re adding today and in the future.
Also, there is a sea shanty, because why shouldn’t there be a sea shanty?
Ahoy there, folks! I’m the Captain of Age of Wonders 4, a game we’ve been sharing with you for either four years or twenty-seven years, depending on how long you’ve been playing the series. Everyone here at Triumph Studios has spent a lifetime coming up with fantastical ideas to add to our games, but now that Age of Wonders 4 is entering its fourth year and kicking off its fourth set of expansions, it’s officially the longest-running title in the franchise in terms of ongoing support.
It makes me proud to work on a game whose players are still hungry for more new stuff, from dragons to vampires to otherworldly terrors beyond comprehension. It makes me even more proud to have players who are so enthusiastic that we have enough great suggestions and ideas from all of you that we can make entire expansions themed around your requests, which is what The Silver Seas is all about. It’s out today, and it’s loaded with goodies that you’ve asked to see!
Let’s start with Pirates. Age of Wonders 4 is a game where your empires and armies sprawl across forests, deserts, underground caverns, on land and at sea, but our players have been asking for more seabound gameplay since launch. Of course, you all made it very clear that you didn’t want to expand onto the sea without being able to build your own swashbuckling pirate fantasies in the process, so we started there. The heart of The Silver Seas is the new Mercantile Culture, which allows you to place cities at sea, and transform them into floating fortresses to rule the waves. We built around two different “flavors” of piracy, adding the Cartel, who grow through smuggling and secrecy, and the Barony, who use their lavish fortunes to place bounties on their enemies and import whatever their empire needs.
Of course, we couldn’t do an aquatic expansion without adding some watery new forms for your people to take. The Silver Seas comes with Sharkkin and Aqualon, two seafaring people who are both, believe it or not, based on player suggestions in their own ways. The Aqualon made their debut (sort of) as a piece of concept art that we shared with our community while working on the Eldritch Realms expansion. So many of you commented that it was a unique and intriguing design that we decided to dive back in and explore what they might become! As for the Sharkkin, every time we’ve asked players what sort of new people we ought to add to the game, there has always been a healthy portion of “Sharks!” in the responses.
Now that we can see how that looks, yeah, fair enough; you were right. Just look at these smiling faces.
Once we had all of these ideas to build out The Silver Seas, the rest came together with designs that just made sense. If we’re going to play out in the water, we ought to add a Magic Tome that uses water magic, and ice magic is a natural progression for water magic. We didn’t add any vapor magic this time around, but who knows? We also added new Pirate Dwellings and pirate-themed stories, terrifying sea creatures to battle, and so much more.
I especially want to thank all of our players for these ideas because it’s not just all of you who get to enjoy playing your Inner Pirate selves. We’ve been indulging in all things buccaneer and swashbuckler here at Triumph, and it’s finally given us an excuse to write a Sea Shanty for work. As you sail The Silver Seas, may this tune keep your compass straight and your sails full. We’ll be seeing ye, me hearties!

items.title: Cougar DuoAir Review – Glass or Mesh?
items.content:
The Cougar DuoAir gets its slightly clunky name from the inclusion of two front panels in the package. The default panel is clear glass but you can switch to the alternate metal mesh panel in a matter of moments. No matter which panel you select the two 140mm ARGB fans in the front of the case shine through brightly and the overall effect of our finished PC is utterly blingtastic.
Timestamps
00:00 Intro
00:34 A slight logistics issue…
01:38 Key features of the DuoAir
02:42 A quick teardown
05:17 Building the PC
07:17 Smoke airflow tests
07:54 Thermal + acoustic tests
10:22 Pricing discussion + closing thoughts
Main features
Interchangeable glass/mesh front panels allow for easy transition between maximum cooling and premium build visibility.
A front-mounted PSU placement clears space for true vertical intake.
Perforated bottom side panels significantly enhance lower fan intake.
Pre-installed 5-fan configuration: 2x 140mm ARGB front fans, 1x 120mm ARGB rear fan, and 2x 120mm bottom fans.
Premium ZPX/ZPB fans utilise Rifle Bearing and stabilising rings to reduce turbulence and ensure silent, long-lasting operation.
Accommodates large 410mm GPUs while maintaining a compact overall footprint.
Refined rounded edges offer a modern alternative aesthetic and gentler handling.
Three integrated dust filters, including a stylish quick-slide front filter, provide effortless maintenance and long-term protection.
A discreetly positioned ARGB light bar adds ambience without disrupting front profile.
Specification:
Motherboard support: ATX, Micro-ATX, Mini-ITX.
Power supply support: ATX.
Expansion slots: 7.
Included fans: 2x 140mm ZPX ARGB 1,800rpm front intake, 1x 120mm 2,200rpm ZPX ARGB rear exhaust, 2x 120mm 2,200rpm ZPB floor intake.
Fan mounts: 2x 140mm front, 2x 140mm/3x 120mm roof, 1x 120mm/140mm rear, 2x 120mm floor.
Radiator mounts: 280mm/360mm roof.
5.25-inch optical drive bays: None.
Internal drive bays: 2x 3.5-inch or 1x 3.5-inch and 2x 2.5-inch.
Front I/O ports: 2x USB 3.0 Type-A, 1x USB 3.2 2×2 Type-C, audio.
Dimensions: 479mm H x 460mm D x 220mm W.
Testing
To put this case through its cooling paces we will be using a test system consisting of an AMD Ryzen 7 9850X3D, Sapphire RX 9070 XT and an SSD. This system allows us to produce a substantial amount of heat and effectively test the Cougar DuoAir‘s cooling capabilities.
Test System:
Processor: AMD Ryzen 7 9850X3D
CPU Cooler: Montech HyperFlow ARGB 360
Motherboard: Sapphire Nitro+ X870EA PhantomLink Polar Edition
Memory: 32GB G.Skill Trident Z5 NeoX RGB DDR5-6000
Graphics card: Sapphire Nitro+ AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT 16GB
Power supply: Fractal Design Ion 3 Gold 1000W
SSD: Crucial T700 Gen 5 M.2 NVMe
OS: Windows 11
Cooling Performance
Cooling Performance Overview
We saw a spread of 10 degrees C in CPU temperatures during our testing which is a very significant figure. Running the fans at a low speed so they are nice and quiet leads to a slightly hot PC, however increasing fan speeds to the maximum is horribly noisy. Our conclusion is that most people should use the mesh front panel and ignore the glass alternative, and that you should run the fans between 1,000rpm and 1,500rpm so you get a decent balance of noise to performance.
Closing Thoughts
The headline feature of the Cougar DuoAir is the choice of mesh or glass front panel and while it is a nice touch we consider it is a minor matter. The glass looks nice enough however the mesh also looks good and performs significantly better while also giving you a full ARGB light show. In our opinion the only reason to stick with the glass is an aesthetic choice as mesh is better in every practical sense.
Beyond that the DuoAir is solidly built and is supplied with five fans which means you have the minimum of assembly to perform when you build your PC. The fundamentals of this case are absolutely sound and Cougar has made no grievous errors or poor choices. The biggest compliment we can pay the DuoAir is that it looks entirely conventional while managing to tuck away a few neat touches just below the surface.
You will be able to buy the Cougar DuoAir for US$89.99.
Pros:
Smart looks with clean styling.
It’s clever without being too clever.
The graphics card cooling system works well.
Cons:
Cable management space is tight.
The location of the front IO lends itself to having your PC on your desk.
There is no separate fan rack in the top of the case.
Does not support rear connection motherboards.
KitGuru says: Cougar DuoAir focuses on airflow to your graphics card, and also delivers an impressive ARGB light show from the fans and front panel.

items.title: Helldivers 2: new poisonous Terminid types, more bug caves spawn across the galaxy today
items.content:
Attention, Helldivers.
The Ministry of Truth confirms that a new Terminid strain is skittering across the front lines. Designated the Noxious strain, these menaces are fast, venomous, and fundamentally opposed to Managed Democracy.
Play Video
Worse still, the bugs have been digging. Terminid cave networks now course beneath more biomes in the galaxy from scorched deserts to frozen tundras. Every planet may have a hive beneath it.
Here is everything a Helldiver needs to know courtesy of the Ministry of Truth:
Noxious Scavenger: small, fast, and full of venom
At first glance these resemble ordinary Scavengers. Their additional vileness becomes more apparent when they skitter in to attack.
Noxious Scavengers are noticeably quicker than their cousins which makes them hard to keep in your sights. Every bite delivers a deadly dose of poison and they are ready to bite again almost immediately. Fortunately, they are fragile. Weapons that reward volume over precision such as shotguns, flamethrowers, and grenades, will make short work of them. Super Earth reminds you that ammunition is cheaper than antivenom.
Noxious Spewer: the big one
Forget everything you know about Spewers dragging themselves across the ground. The Noxious Spewer is a hulking monstrosity that moves with unsettling speed and it is responsible for the webs now draped across the battlefield.
At medium range, watch for its Web Spit. One hit and you lose the ability to sprint, which is exactly what the abomination wants: to slow its prey and close the gap. Beware its bite, which is quick, has surprising reach, and carries a stronger dose of venom than anything a Scavenger can deliver.
While its head is protected by medium armor, its web-filled abdomen has no armor at all. Be cautious when targeting this location, as when the sac bursts in a Web Explosion, it will snare every Helldiver and bug nearby. Super Earth recommends not being caught in the explosion.
Noxious venom: All sorts of bad news
Every Noxious bite inflicts poison, which can cripple the Democratic spirit of even the most stalwart Helldivers. You can track your condition with the new poison icon on your HUD. Super Earth categorizes the poisoning as follows:
Lightly poisoned: Your vision starts to haze, the poison begins to eat away at your health
Heavily poisoned: Damage over time increases, you lose the ability to sprint, your vision hazes, Lady Liberty comes to visit you
Thankfully, your stims will help cure your condition, so ration them wisely. A poisoned squadmate may need that stim to keep going and fulfill your mission.
Caves on more biomes
The Terminids have gone underground and Super Earth is hunting them down. Bug caves are no longer limited to a handful of worlds; they now have a chance to appear across more biomes on the Galactic map.
Inside these tunnels sightlines are short, corners are blind, and fast enemies arrive before you hear them. Absolutely ideal territory for those Noxious bugs. Bring close-range firepower, stay with your squad, and keep a stim in reserve for whoever wandered too far ahead.
Suit up, Helldiver
The Noxious strain want the galaxy wrapped in silk and soaked in venom. Super Earth has other plans, and those plans involve you.
Pack your stims, aim for the abdomen, and remember: arachnophobia is not a recognized exemption from military service. See you in the caves, Helldiver. Remember, a cleaner galaxy starts with YOU, Helldiver.
A cleaner galaxy starts with YOU.

items.title: SteamOS now runs on Apple Silicon thanks to new open-source project
items.content:
An open-source project called FX Steam Launcher is bringing SteamOS to Apple Silicon Macs. Rather than replacing macOS, the software runs Valve's ARM64 version of SteamOS inside a virtual machine, allowing Mac users to access SteamOS, Proton and a growing number of Windows-compatible games.
As demonstrated by ETAPrime (via VideoCardz), early testing has produced surprisingly promising results. Running on a MacBook Pro equipped with an M4 Max chip, Left 4 Dead 2 exceeded 200FPS, while Stellar Blade and The Witcher 3 both reportedly ran at over 70FPS using the SteamOS virtual machine.
The project relies on Valve's official ARM64 version of SteamOS, with Windows game compatibility handled through Proton and additional translation layers that convert x86 code and DirectX instructions for Apple Silicon hardware. The software can run in either a window or fullscreen mode while retaining audio and controller support.
The project remains a work in progress, however. Testing revealed graphical glitches, shader compilation stutter and compatibility issues in some games, with titles including DOOM Eternal, Ghost of Tsushima and Marvel's Spider-Man: Miles Morales failing to launch correctly. Earlier testing on a Mac mini with 16GB of memory also highlighted performance limitations when system memory became constrained.
KitGuru says: SteamOS running on Apple Silicon felt like a long shot not too long ago. Would you be tempted to use a SteamOS VM on your Mac for gaming?

items.title: Phantom Blade Zero officially sells 4 million copies in 3 days
items.content:
Almost a decade on from its initial inception, the fast-paced action-RPG Phantom Blade Zero is finally here. While it was clear that the game had amassed a major audience from the get-go (achieving a peak concurrent player count of 800,000 on Steam alone), studio S-GAME has now come out with an even more impressive figure – revealing that Phantom Blade Zero has officially sold 4 million copies in its first 3 days.
Taking to Twitter to make the announcement, studio S-GAME officially revealed just how successful the game has been during its first few days on the market, stating: “Phantom Blade Zero has sold over 4 million copies in just 72 hours! Thank you everyone from the bottom of our hearts for all the love and support!”
As mentioned, it was quite clear from early on that Phantom Blade Zero was going to have a strong launch, with the game’s director revealing back in September that the title had amassed more than 3 million wishlists.
Of course, wishlists are just that – wishlists – and so the real question which remained was how many of those 3 million would wind up purchasing the actual game. As it turns out, all of them and then some.
While not quite a 1:1 comparison, 2024’s Black Myth Wukong (which initially launched on both PC and PS5) sold a total of 10 million copies within its first 3 days on the market. So, while Phantom Blade Zero is still a far cry from the behemoth that was Black Myth Wukong, the latter remains one of the fastest-selling games of all time, and so being in the conversion at all is an achievement in and of itself.
Regardless, with incredibly strong early sales and an aggregate review score quite a bit higher than Wukong, it may not be long before Phantom Blade Zero manages to surpass another major milestone.

items.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 (2009) appears on game ratings board
items.content:
Earlier this year, during the mid-way point in Call of Duty: Black Ops 7’s lifecycle, Activision announced and released current-gen ports for both Black Ops 1 and 2 for PlayStation, marking the first time that PS4/5 owners have been able to play either game on their system (due to the lack of backwards compatibility with PS3). It appears as though something similar might be happening with the OG Modern Warfare 2 – as the 2009 classic has now popped up on the Australian games rating board.
As reported by multiple users, the Australian Classifications board recently published a new listing for Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 (2009). As of now, the listing does not include too much in the way of details, and so it is unknown whether this port will be exclusive to PlayStation (as was the case with BO1+2).
That said, what is clear is the fact that this port appears to be the full MW2 experience, with the rating making explicit note of “Online Interactivity and Chat” – meaning unlike 2020’s Modern Warfare 2 Campaign Remastered, this release should include the game’s iconic multiplayer modes.
In a less positive comparison to Campaign Remastered however, this port is likely to be just that: a port, meaning players can expect pretty much the exact same visuals and settings as the PS3 original (meaning 60fps and a low-FOV) albeit at a slightly higher resolution.
Regardless, given the fact that the aforementioned BO1+2 ports ended up selling over 11 million copies in its first month alone, it’s safe to assume that Activision will port over all of the 7th-gen Call of Duty offerings eventually.

Since his earliest days tinkering with Windows 95 on a classic Pentium MMX PC, Ben’s been obsessed with understanding how technology works, chatting about it with anyone who’ll listen. Along the way, he’s worked as a UK college lecturer, teaching IT to adults and teenagers, and as a PC technician, tackling all kinds of tech problems. He’s now busy tracking down brilliant bargains on all kinds of hardware, but when he doesn’t have his deal hat on, he’s adding to his homelab, watching old Star Trek episodes, or taking two hyperactive pugs on a much needed walk.

items.title: ‘Until Dawn 2 Live’ presentation announced for December
items.content:
More than a decade on from the first game’s release, the campy interactive horror adventure Until Dawn is set to receive a sequel. Officially arriving on the 28th of January, the cogs in Sony’s marketing machine have started to turn, with the console manufacturer announcing a ‘live’ presentation featuring gameplay for Until Dawn 2, set to take place next month.
Taking to Twitter to make the announcement, the official PlayStation page revealed that they will be hosting an in-person event in anticipation of the upcoming Until Dawn 2, writing:
“Until Dawn 2 comes to Alamo Drafthouse on December 11 for exclusive gameplay, a horror movie marathon, and special talent appearances. More details on the event and livestream coming soon.”
Serving as a bit of multi-media marketing, this is not the first time that PlayStation has partnered with the Alamo Drafthouse, with its screens being used for various PlayStation presentations in the past.
Regardless of whether you watch in-person or online, the upcoming livestream should give us our best look yet at the game. Of course, the original Until Dawn was not a gameplay-focused experience, and so it will be interesting to see how different the sequel will choose to approach this aspect of the game.
Based on the footage shared so far, Until Dawn 2 does appear to be in-line mechanically with the first game. That said, with new studio Firespite in charge this time round, things could be quite different. We will have to wait until next month to find out.
KitGuru says: What do you think of the trailers released so far? Do you think Until Dawn 2 will introduce new gameplay elements compared to Supermassive Games’ offerings? Let us know down below.

items.title: Square Enix originally wanted Final Fantasy Resonance to be a “simple port”
items.content:
Following a decade of operation, Square Enix officially shut down the mobile-exclusive Final Fantasy: Brave Exvius last year. That said, the game would later be revived and rebuilt in Square’s signature HD-2D art style for PC and consoles under the name Final Fantasy Resonance. Commenting on the title’s early success, producer Keisuke Nakashima revealed that Square Enix initially just wanted to do “a simple port.”
Officially launched on the 22nd of October, Final Fantasy Resonance has been met with a great deal of positivity, amassing a Metacritic score of 86 and an ‘Overwhelmingly Positive’ reception on Steam.
While the game is based on the bones of 2015’s mobile exclusive FF: Brave Exvius, Resonance was pretty much entirely rebuilt – most noticeably when it comes to the game’s art style, arriving as the first Final Fantasy title to make use of Square’s HD-2D aesthetic.
According to the game’s producer ‘Keisuke Nakashima’ however, this wasn’t always the case. In an interview with the publication Bloomberg (paywalled) and as reported by NintendoEverything, Nakashima revealed that “initially there was some resistance to the idea from Square Enix executives”, with the higher-ups wanting a more basic port.
As claimed by Nakashima: “I didn’t want to go down that route. I wanted to create an original version for consoles that was a full-blown gameplay experience.”
Part of the mentality behind this reimagining came due to the producer's desire to remove Brave Exvius’ gacha mechanics from Resonance, claiming that “It was really disappointing to hear people didn’t want to play it just because of the gacha elements. That was another reason we wanted to make this a console game, to bring it to a wider audience.”
Whether it be the lack of gacha, the embrace of HD-2D or a combination of multiple factors, Final Fantasy Resonance appears to be a success on all fronts. It will be interesting to see what lessons Square Enix will take away from this.
KitGuru says: Have you checked out Final Fantasy Resonance? What do you think of it? How does it compare to Brave Exvius in your opinion? Let us know down below.

October Steam Survey reverses many of September’s biggest shifts
items.content:
Valve has published its October 2026 Steam Hardware & Software Survey results, and many of last month's most dramatic changes have already begun to reverse. Several categories that saw unusually large shifts in September, including memory capacity, GPU market share and language distribution, have largely moved back towards their previous positions.
September's survey saw 32GB of RAM briefly overtake 16GB as the most common memory configuration among Steam users, while the GeForce RTX 5070 surged ahead of the RTX 3060. October's results tell a different story. 16GB has regained the top spot at 41.42%, up 3.60 percentage points month-on-month, while 32GB fell 5.16 points to 37.06%. The RTX 3060 has also reclaimed its position as Steam's most popular graphics card at 3.62%, narrowly ahead of the RTX 5070 at 3.56%.
The most likely explanation appears to be a change in survey demographics rather than a sudden shift in purchasing behaviour. Simplified Chinese users accounted for 21.98% of survey responses in October, down 9.41 percentage points from the previous month. Meanwhile, English-language users increased by 4.84 percentage points to 39.04%, helping to explain why several hardware categories appear to have swung back towards earlier trends.
Elsewhere, Windows 11 continued its steady rise, gaining 1.17 percentage points to reach 72.51% of surveyed systems. Intel also extended its lead among Windows CPU users, increasing its share to 53.48%, while AMD slipped to 46.51%. The survey also showed Linux growing to 3.95% of systems, although Windows remains overwhelmingly dominant among Steam users.
KitGuru says: September's Steam Survey always looked a little unusual. Do October's results paint a more accurate picture of the current PC gaming market?

items.title: Cities Worldwide Build and Scale AI Services With NVIDIA Physical and Agentic AI
items.content:
Cities generate enormous amounts of data from cameras, sensors and operational systems, but turning it into useful action — for planning, maintenance and public services — remains a challenge.
Physical and agentic AI offer new ways to close that gap, from digital twins for infrastructure planning to vision and service agents, while keeping local governments in control of how sensitive data is processed and used.
Building on initiatives announced at GTC Berlin, NVIDIA and its partners are expanding physical AI and AI agents to cities worldwide. Shared computing infrastructure gives city departments, neighboring municipalities and local developers a common foundation to build on — extending services without each organization having to acquire and manage resources of their own.
Agentic AI for Cities
From resident services to vision agents, cities are adopting NVIDIA agentic AI to deliver faster, more responsive public services. City teams don’t need a massive infrastructure investment to get started building these AI services: depending on the workload, NVIDIA RTX workstations or a small GPU system may be enough.
In Spain, 1MillionBot combines open source ALIA models trained at the Barcelona Supercomputing Center with NVIDIA Nemotron and other models in resident-service agents for Madrid Digital (Comunidad de Madrid), Administració Oberta de Catalunya and 150+ deployments across Spain, handling municipal procedures, appointment requests, urban-planning incidents and service inquiries.
In the San Francisco Bay Area, LiveX is bringing its AI City vision to life with NVIDIA Cosmos world models and Nemotron open models, and Omniverse and Metropolis libraries on NVIDIA RTX PRO GPUs. The interactive, conversational AI hosts understand people’s needs, provide answers and take action, and can be tailored to local languages and service needs in airports, hospitals, local events and other public spaces.
Vision AI agents can turn existing city camera feeds into operational insights, helping teams identify mobility and safety issues and coordinate emergency responses across city services.
In Wrocław, Poland, K2K is building shared AI infrastructure using NVIDIA accelerated computing, NVIDIA Cosmos world reasoning models, and NVIDIA Metropolis Blueprint for video search and summarization (VSS) to transform existing camera streams into actionable intelligence for mobility, safety and event response — using the same infrastructure across several city functions.
In Malaysia, ITMAX bundles infrastructure and agentic AI applications into long-term managed services for cities, including for traffic management. Built with reference to Cosmos, Nemotron and the Metropolis VSS blueprint, ITMAX’s SamurAI V2 vision agents are scaling on NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 GPUs to support 17,000+ cameras by 2027. ITMAX integrates TeraSim, an open source traffic simulation platform from Laplace Intelligence, to test signal timing, reducing peak-hour corridor travel times by up to 26%.
Plan and Operate Critical Infrastructure With Digital Twins
Beyond public-facing services, digital twins can help cities expedite infrastructure planning, minimizing disruption to local communities. City digital twins can also serve as a real-time operational simulation to facilitate faster decision-making.
At Dangote’s Lekki refinery in Nigeria, Honeywell Technologies’ Forge Plant Cognition uses Nemotron-powered AI agents to understand operational data. A digital twin of the plant and its processes, built using Omniverse libraries, is also planned to support simulation and training. The platform, built on Dell PowerEdge servers with NVIDIA RTX PRO accelerators, helps operators identify bottlenecks, anticipate equipment and process issues, and optimize plant performance.
In Taiwan, Linker Vision and Dutch architecture firm MVRDV are using NVIDIA Omniverse and Nemotron to build environmental, social and governance agents that can assess the environmental impact of various urban planning scenarios, simulating 15-year outcomes of an urban forest canopy in 10 minutes — increasing design iteration speed from two weeks per iteration to less than an hour.
Build a Broader Local AI Ecosystem
Cities can extend AI to more services by building on infrastructure already in place and adding capacity. Shared resources and managed services can help extend those capabilities across departments and municipalities.
At Morocco’s Tanger Med port, Cires Technologies is expanding a sovereign AI factory for planned applications in worker safety, congestion analysis, cargo routing and port operations. Cires Technologies is also building an ecosystem of application providers to develop local models and applications for ports and cities.
Beyond city services, Barcelona Supercomputing Center’s AI Factory Accelerator Programme gives startups access to sovereign computing, technical support and training. BSC AI Factory also supports research and innovation for startups — spanning agriculture, medical imaging, knowledge access and speech services.
Learn how NVIDIA and its ecosystem are bringing physical AI, agentic AI and local AI factories to cities worldwide at Smart City Expo World Congress, running Nov. 3-5 in Barcelona, where NVIDIA Vice President of EMEA Paolo Guglielmini will deliver a keynote address followed by a panel moderated by Charbel Aoun, director of smart city and spaces for EMEA at NVIDIA.

items.title: Borderlands franchise surpasses 100M copies sold as Gearbox teases future plans
items.content:
The Borderlands franchise has officially surpassed 100 million copies sold, a milestone reached more than 17 years after the release of the original game. Alongside the announcement, Gearbox has also begun teasing its long-term plans for the series following the completion of Borderlands 4's first year of post-launch content.
First released in 2009, Borderlands helped popularise the looter shooter genre and has since grown into one of 2K's biggest gaming franchises. The series now spans multiple mainline entries, spin-offs and expansions, with Borderlands 4 serving as the latest chapter following its launch just over a year ago.
Gearbox also used the milestone announcement to look back on Borderlands 4's first year of support. Since launch, the game has received two Story Packs, five Bounty Packs, two additional Vault Hunters, two free Raid Boss encounters, an endgame Takedown activity and a range of quality-of-life improvements and gameplay updates. The studio confirmed that weekly activity refreshes and community challenges will continue, with additional Borderlands 4 content planned for 2027.
Perhaps more interestingly, Gearbox hinted at a broader future for the franchise beyond its current content roadmap. In a message to players, the studio said it is exploring new character arcs, storylines and the overall direction of the Borderlands universe. While no new projects were announced, the comments suggest that planning for the next phase of the franchise is already underway.

items.title: World of Warcraft: Forever – How Controller Support Reimagines the Way We Can Play in Azeroth
items.content:
My approach to World of Warcraft has largely been one of logging in and enjoying a casual adventure in Azeroth. I’m not messing around with macros or trying to carry a team through a dungeon. I’m more than happy to spend my time chewing on scenery and gobbling up lore. Yes, I’m that guy that wants to know exactly why he must fell 15 trolls.
This taps into one of the many things that makes World of Warcraft great, in that Blizzard wants to make sure there’s a WoW experience that suits everybody. Whether it’s through PC hardware support, innovations in battle mechanics like Single-Button Assistant, and rolling out numerous accessibility features such as Text to Speech, the game constantly hits it out of the park for creating a world for so many players to access and enjoy.
This is one of the things that has made me excited for World of Warcraft: Forever, in that Blizzard can now take all the years of learned knowledge of creating a welcoming Azeroth and return us to an age when it still felt fresh and unknown; like an adventure every time you logged in – and now we’ll be able to play with a controller in our hands thanks to Gamepad (Alpha) support.
Vanilla Ice Cream
I suppose I should back up just a bit to give you a refresher on what World of Warcraft: Forever is and why it’s a pretty big deal. Essentially, we’ll return to a version of the game’s world that is very similar to the WoW that arrived in 2004, but with many new stories, locations, and improved features that work to strike that middle ground between that Classic feel, mixed with added improvements to make the experience welcoming for newcomers. And it’s going to stay that way, hence the Forever in the game’s title.
What does that mean lore-wise? We’re back to the two main continents, Eastern Kingdoms and Kalimdor, and the classic races featuring humans, orcs, elves, trolls, dwarfs, and others. But don’t expect a 1:1 experience as there will still be a lot of new to explore. The most significant are the Skyborne, a new race of elves that occupy the recently uncovered floating Zephras Isle.
Back on the ground, there will be new areas to discover in the Riverglades and Mount Hyjal, improved lighting and graphics to make familiar locations feel new, as well as revamps to class combos, like being able to roll with a Forsaken Paladin.
Think of Forever as filling the gaps of Azeroth with denser content to keep the Classic vibes in play. And it’s all included in your current subscription, so there’s no additional purchase required to experience this old-new world. And one of those new ways to experience Azeroth will influence not only how to play but also where.
Couch Surfing
My personal PC gaming rig is about the size of a game console, which occasionally finds a home next to my XBOX Series X|S in the living room; I’m rocking an AMD Ryzen 7 7800X3D and ASUS Prime Radeon RX 9070 all in a small form factor Fractal Ridge case. Now with World of Warcraft: Forever and its Gamepad (Alpha) support, I’m as close as I’ve ever been to a console-like Warcraft experience – and it’s awesome.
Consider using Compact Action Bar to free up screen space from the UI.
Enabling the controller support is seamless from the main menu – just go into Options and check the box for “Gamepad (Alpha)” support. That will change your on-screen icons to match your controller’s buttons and from there you can start adventuring. I would recommend a modern XBOX Wireless Controller to use since every on-screen button icon maps perfectly.
The first thing I wanted to work out with the Gamepad (Alpha) feature was accessing my normal routines – how to access Bags; where are my Quests; how do I look at my character? This has come together over time. I haven’t found anything that I can’t access through just the controller, and that’s a good thing for this feature’s future support.
I recommend a modern XBOX Wireless Controller to use since every on-screen button icon maps perfectly.
Like learning the controls of any new role-playing game, there’s a certain rhythm you’ll become accustomed to with combat. For those who have already been playing World of Warcraft for a long time, you’ll have the added benefit of understanding how character progression, buffs, order of attacks, and additional skills will unlock. I will say that combat in Forever feels more rhythmic than modern Warcraft, which leans in the controller support’s favor, giving you a little bit more time to think through your next attack.
Combat itself involves cycling through actions tied to the controller’s Triggers and Bumpers, which when pressed alternate the actions that are mapped to your controller’s buttons. Once I got that hang of it, I was really moving into a nice combat flow, triggering enemies, casting spells, running away, and more.
Nudge others in your party on with commands like, Attack, Warning, On My Way, and Assist.
What I’m still working on is interacting with other players with just the controller. There is a ping system tied to holding down the right analog stick that can help you nudge others in your party on with commands like, Attack, Warning, On My Way, and Assist, but having a keyboard and/or voice chat still feels like the way to go. Having my wireless keyboard next to me on the couch is a good fallback option.
Warcraft Forever, Wherever
Another fun piece of PC gaming hardware I’m fortunate to have on hand is an ASUS ROG XBOX Ally. As fellow owners know, it features a lot of customization options to get most modern games running on it in some capacity. And since it runs Windows 11, apps like Battle.net can run on it too. So that got me thinking – could I get World of Warcraft: Forever running on it too? Yes, I could.
Use the UI’s Edit Mode and adjust to your liking.
There is a bit of a caveat though, in that it takes some patience to get there. And it isn’t officially supported yet, but by using a mix of the system’s touchscreen and onscreen keyboard, you can navigate to the main menu to toggle the Gamepad (Alpha) controller support feature.
I’d also recommend taking a few minutes to go into the UI’s Edit Mode and reduce the size of the Chat Frame and lowering the Player and Targeting Frames to the bottom of the screen to give you some more visibility to the action on the screen. The default positioning of the Gamepad Action Bar is pretty good, but consider checking the box to use Compact Action Bar to free up some more of that screen space from the UI. After that it’s a pretty seamless gameplay experience in your hands comparable to my time playing Forever on my couch.
Throughout the beta leading up to launch, I would swap between playing on desktop, couch, and handheld with Forever and it has been a delight in experimenting with first-party controller support for one of my favorite games. I never thought I’d be able to lay back in bed with a handheld and play World of Warcraft, or lounge back on the couch while running a dungeon, but here we are!
Excitement around World of Warcraft: Forever is palpable. On November 4, PC players can return to a nostalgic world many grew up with – and others will discover for the first time – now with the freedom to play wherever and whenever they choose with the addition of Gamepad (Alpha) support. Forever has reimagined a way for us to explore Azeroth in more ways than one, and I can’t wait to dive in. Again.
The post World of Warcraft: Forever – How Controller Support Reimagines the Way We Can Play in Azeroth appeared first on XBOX Wire.

items.title: Persona 1 remake apparently revealed through leaked trailer
items.content:
A newly leaked trailer appears to show Atlus' next Persona remake project. Following Persona 3 Reload and a Persona 4 remake due in early 2027, the publisher now looks to be revisiting the very first entry in the series.
The trailer has begun circulating online ahead of any official announcement and appears to show gameplay from a remake of the original Persona. While Atlus has yet to comment on the footage, the leak includes combat sequences, exploration and a fully realised user interface.
As with any leak, there is no way to immediately verify its authenticity. The footage could be an elaborate fan-made project, although there are several details that make it difficult to dismiss outright. Alongside gameplay footage and completed menu systems, the trailer also appears to contain work-in-progress story segments using what look to be storyboard placeholders rather than final assets.
If legitimate, the remake would continue Atlus' recent effort to modernise older entries in the series. Persona 3 Reload was followed by plans for a Persona 4 remake, while Persona 6 remains in development for a later release. A remake of the original game would make sense given comments from Atlus producers in recent years expressing interest in revisiting Persona's earliest entries.
The original Persona launched for the PlayStation in 1996 under the title Revelations: Persona in Western markets. While later games in the series became global hits, the first entry has largely remained locked to older platforms, receiving just one major re-release via the PSP in 2009.

Gang of Dragon studio closes just one year after game reveal
items.content:
Yakuza creator Toshihiro Nagoshi's new studio is shutting down, just 11 months after unveiling its debut game, Gang of Dragon. The closure means the Sleeping Dogs and Yakuza-inspired action title has effectively been cancelled before it ever reached players.
Nagoshi Studio was founded in 2021 after Toshihiro Nagoshi's departure from Sega, with financial backing from NetEase. The studio finally unveiled its first project, Gang of Dragon, during The Game Awards 2025, presenting it as a gritty action game starring actor Ma Dong-seok. At the time, the project appeared to be a major new venture from one of Japan's most recognisable game creators.
However, the studio's future reportedly came into question earlier this year when Bloomberg reported that NetEase planned to end funding for the project as part of broader cutbacks to its games business. According to the report, the publisher baulked after learning that Gang of Dragon would need an additional ¥7 billion (around $44M) to reach completion.
Now, Japanese publication 4Gamer reports that shareholders voted to dissolve Nagoshi Studio during a meeting held on the 31st of October. While no formal cancellation announcement for Gang of Dragon has been issued, the closure of the studio effectively brings development of the project to an end.

Final Fantasy XIV: Evercold delayed into crowded February 2027 release window
items.content:
Final Fantasy XIV players will have to wait a little longer for Evercold. Square Enix has delayed the MMORPG's next expansion from its planned January release window, pushing the launch back by a few weeks to the 23rd of February 2027.
Speaking during the Final Fantasy XIV Fan Festival (via MMORPG), producer and director Naoki Yoshida explained that the team had been pushing to meet its original target, but ultimately needed additional time to hit the quality bar expected for a major expansion release.
Yoshida said he personally made the decision to delay the launch, despite the project being relatively close to its original schedule. Players who pre-order Evercold from the 4th of November will gain access to the expansion's early access period, which begins on the 19th of February.
A delay of just a few weeks may not seem significant, but it means Evercold is moving from what looked like a relatively quiet January launch window into an increasingly crowded February. The expansion will now release alongside new entries for some of the gaming industry's biggest franchises, including titles like Fable, Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis and God of War Laufey, all of which are currently targeting February launches of their own.

‘90s style sci-fi horror Derelikt launches Nov 13 on PS5
items.content:
Back in 1999, gaming was good. Games that were released late in the original PlayStation generation squeezed the last drop of performance out of the hardware, resulting in impressive visuals and all-time classics whose sequels we still play today. Fast forward 26 years and we’re excited to announce that our sci-fi horror game Derelikt will make you feel like your console shed 5 generations when it launches on PlayStation 5 on November 13.
Play Video
Derelikt takes place aboard Von Neumann Outpost, grafted onto an anomalous asteroid discovered in Saturn’s orbit. Things are rough. The work is hard, home is a million miles away, and people are stressed out. Plus, a mysterious drone is driving everyone closer to their breaking point…
You arrive as an outside contractor tasked with finding out the fate of Excavation Team Delta, who went missing on the derelict surface. What you discover turns things from bad to worse fast! The halls are dark, the systems are failing, and the survivors that you come across aren’t telling the same story. Nailing that feeling of not being able to trust those around you, while simultaneously coming face to face with truly out-of-this-world horrors, was paramount for us.
The Von Neumann Outpost is well stocked with an arsenal of traditional weapons, and as you progress, you might even find a few more outlandish weapon prototypes and even alien weapons at your disposal. There are also over a dozen to interact with in Derelikt, each featuring their own secrets, and agendas. Some are useful, some are dangerous, some are doomed, and some (let’s be real, most) are all three!
We wanted to not only create this horrifyingly tense world full of scary moments and fast gunplay, but also make sure to make managing resources, exploration, dialogues and old-school puzzle solving a core part of the tension experience.
Derelikt is very much inspired by the PSOne-era of sci-fi horror, and it feels like a full-circle moment to be writing this today. The goal was to make it appear as if we found Derelikt on a CD-R in the dusty, long-abandoned storage unit of a defunct late-90s developer and simply ported it to modern platforms. I’m of the firm opinion that retro doesn’t have to mean crude and primitive, and I set out to create the most faithful homage to 5th generation graphics available on the market.
Our game features 100% lovingly hand-painted textures and vertex colour lighting. Affine Texture warping was deliberately implemented and mitigated in the next step by dynamically subdividing the geometry – just like the most high-end games of the era did – and the game also features retro-style full-motion CGI cutscenes. This way, a delicate balance was achieved – Derelikt looks aesthetically pleasing while still conceivably plausible on period hardware. Our team made a conscious effort to implement modern game design while keeping the core feeling and charm of that era of sci-fi horror intact, including an option for players to toggle on or off effects to match their particular taste.
Derelikt has been in development in some form since late 2021 and has had a turbulent and exciting development journey. We hope the game is as wild a ride for players as it has been to develop!

Buyers looking to upgrade to an OLED gaming monitor this year can now pick up a free PC game at the same time. MSI's latest UK promotion includes some of the biggest games of the year, with titles like 007 First Light, The Blood of Dawnwalker, Resident Evil Requiem and Silent Hill: Townfall available to claim with selected QD-OLED monitors and gaming desktops.
The promotion runs from the 1st of November through to the 31st of December and is available across a wide range of MSI displays and systems. MSI has also added two gaming desktops to the promotion, with the MPG Infinite X3 AI and MAG Infinite Z qualifying for free game vouchers when purchased through Currys.
To claim a game, customers will need to register their qualifying product through MSI's member programme and submit proof of purchase. Once approved, MSI will issue a Gamesplanet voucher that can be redeemed against a game of the buyer's choice from the promotional catalogue. Claims are available until the 31st of December 2026.

Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered fighter guide
items.content:
With its giant-sized fanbase, Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered has plenty of players ready to get tooth, nail, and claw stuck into its PlayStation 5 release on November 3. Although it would be understandable that newcomers might feel a little intimidated choosing between 12 world crushing kaiju, each with their own stats, moveset, and special abilities. Never fear – we have the rundown on which colossus matches your playstyle to ensure you’re the true king of the monsters.
Heisei Godzilla
Ideal for: Players who want to dive straight in.
The face which sank a thousand ships. Godzilla is the iconic kaiju who all other kaiju want to be, beat, or be friends with. As the game’s default character, the giant lizard is balanced for newbies and veterans alike, with a high amount of starting health and decent all-round stats.
Godzilla also possesses a tail useful enough for a mighty wake-up strike when he’s downed, and some fairly swift claws, so many of his melee combos are effective for beginners. But don’t rely too much on his high-energy pulse – while it’s formidable, the slow charge leaves him open to counters. Similarly, ranged attackers can take advantage of his relatively sluggish projectiles, so close that distance or you’ll be heading back to Monster Island with your giant tail between your legs.
Godzilla 2000
Ideal for: Players annoyed at their friend for picking Heisei Godzilla.
In terms of film history, Godzilla 2000 is a more modern incarnation of the legendary lizard, reflecting a new era for the new millennium. Although he’s arguably a slightly more vulnerable version of his Heisei predecessor.
As a result, while Godzilla 2000 is a bit faster than his kaiju shoto fighter twin, he’s not quite as strong. He’s still fairly well balanced and arguably easier to use than Heisei, so makes for a solid alternative. And his distinctive purple dorsal plates look pretty cool, too.
King Ghidorah
Ideal for: Players who want to control the battlefield.
There’s a reason why this fearsome three-headed beast is seen as Godzilla’s archnemesis. Giant wings, gravity beams, and a desire to annihilate humanity, the threat of King Ghidorah should never be taken lightly.
Given his monstrous size it shouldn’t be a surprise that the ‘supreme ruler of the cosmos’ isn’t the fastest kaiju on the block, but he’s resilient and a perfect ‘zoning’ character, capable of keeping foes at a distance with a variety of projectiles. His flight is a little limited due to its energy drain, but it’s balanced by a lightning blast that has no charge while airborne. However, despite his colossal wings, Ghidorah’s lack of arms and stubby legs makes him a poor melee fighter.
Anguirus
Ideal for: Players who think defense is the best offense.
He might look a bit like Godzooky with more spikes, but mutant dinosaur Anguirus is one of Godzilla’s most loyal allies – even if his track record against other kaiju hasn’t been the best in the movies.
The Monster Island citizen is fast and aggressive, but his low power and lack of long-range attacks means Anguirus is best utilized as a counter-attack specialist. His block might be on the slow side due to its turning animation, but it actually damages an attacking opponent due to Anguirus’ rear spines. With his high defense and solid grappling skills, this mutant shouldn’t be underestimated.
Megalon
Ideal for: Players who love to hit and run.
Given its status as a guardian to the ancient underground civilisation of Seatopia, Megalon is more of an antagonist than an out-and-out villain in Godzilla lore. While not quite as domineering as its colossal rivals, the subterranean kaiju is still capable of putting a hurt on with its drill-like appendages.
Megalon’s primary advantage is its tunnelling skill which not only allows it to avoid attacks, but also pop-up and grab opponents. Even though burrowing uses energy, it still makes Megalon a difficult fighter to pin down, especially when used in tandem with its myriad of electricity attacks. On the flip side, Megalon isn’t the most durable of beasts with below average defense. Stick and move, or die.
Gigan
Ideal for: Players wanting to attack with deadly speed.
One of the most sadistic fighters to hail from M Space Hunter Nebula, cyborg kaiju Gigan is easily one of Godzilla’s more vicious adversaries. Despite being defeated multiple times, the hook-clawed Gigan just keeps coming back for more.
Unsurprisingly, Gigan’s tenacious approach makes him perfect for aggressive rushdown tactics. He’s not only swift, but his teleportation ability gives him incredible range and evasion skills. And those hooks aren’t for decoration either, delivering damage-heavy edged strikes. His Laser Eye is a little unwieldy, and he’s vulnerable to energy attacks, but Gigan remains a versatile option for anyone wanting a decent melee and range mix-up.
Destoroyah
Ideal for: Players wanting a classic tank character.
Known as ‘death incarnate’, everything about Destoroyah is built to intimidate. Giant wings, clawed hands, taloned feet… this mutant crustacean almost has it all.
Which is to say, Destoroyah is one of the more powerful creatures in the game with brutal physical assaults and a wide variety of high-damage – and often unblockable – energy attacks that truly make him the perfect mid-range monster. But there’s a cost. Destoroyah’s best abilities are extremely power hungry, so without them he’s potentially ineffective given how painfully slow his movement is.
Rodan
Ideal for: Players wanting speed above all else.
With his dominance of the skies and fearsome pteranodon looks, you’d be fooled into thinking Rodan is an out-and-out villain, but he’s more a force of chaos, even capable of being selfless in some parts of Godzilla lore.
True to type, Rodan is not only the fastest monster in the game, but also the most mobile in the air. With his powerful breath attack and speedy melee attacks, he’s another great hit-and-run character. However, Rodan has shockingly low durability, with the weakest defense of the entire roster, so going toe-to-toe is not recommended.
Mecha-King Ghidorah
Ideal for: Players wanting a long-range grappler.
When one possible future sees the three-headed beast defeated, his body is salvaged and rebuilt by 23rd century scientists to serve humanity. The result is a cyborg that merges Ghidorah’s ferocity with bionic enhancements, including a shield, and projectiles with draining abilities.
So while Mecha-King Ghidorah doesn’t quite have the raw power of his original form, his weapons are far more useful on a whole, and his grappling versatility is impressive. That said, he’s just as slow, and he relies on energy to maintain his best attacks including his shield, meaning Mecha-King Ghidorah can be vulnerable to powerful prolonged assaults.
Mechagodzilla
Ideal for: Players wanting a heavy duty ranged fighter.
Mechagodzilla is the alien Vortaak’s heavily weaponised answer to the fire-breathing giant lizard, in their attempt to conquer Earth. And with near indestructible space titanium, lasers, missiles, and even a plasma cannon, they’ve left very little to chance.
Unlike its Kiryu sibling, Mechagodzilla is more specialised, with a greater degree of weapons and better defensive stats. And let’s not forget its iconic flying head-butt. Mechagodzilla’s main issue? Its reliance on energy for flying and many of its ranged attacks – so if that’s depleted, the automaton is left with its underwhelming grabs and sluggish melee.
Orga
Ideal for: Players wanting the best grappler in the game.
A terrifying looking alien in its own right, Orga hasn’t many appearances in Godzilla media, but the goliath – mutated from some of Godzilla’s DNA – is able to hold its own… not least due to its venomous maw and gigantic hands.
It’s those mitts which make Orga a menace in the arena, with its long reach offering a massive advantage to close and mid-range confrontations. But while Orga isn’t the slowest of monsters, it’s still relatively sluggish, and limited against anyone resistant to blunt attacks, or too fast for grabs. And as useful as its paralysing goo is, the high energy cost can leave Orga exposed if it misses.
Kiryu
Ideal for: Players needing a more weapons-focused Godzilla.
What do you get when you place the original Godzilla’s skeleton inside of a robot body? In this case, a slightly unstable anti-kaiju cyborg designed to protect humanity. Kiryu (translated into ‘machine dragon” from the original kanji) is one of the more popular iterations of Mechagodzilla, and a heavily armoured walking, flying arsenal.
Compared to Mechagodzilla, Kiryu has better balanced stats, which makes it the optimal choice for those looking for a more weapons-ready, energy hungry version of the base Godzillas, with a punchy rage attack thanks to its Absolute Zero Cannon.
Ready to see if you can keep up with your chosen kaiju? Get smashing when Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered fights its way to PlayStation 5 on November 3.

Soulframe is finally opening its doors to everyone. After years of invite-only testing, Digital Extremes has announced that its fantasy action RPG will enter Open Preludes this week, allowing anyone on PC to jump in and try the game without waiting for an invitation.

Windows 11 Preview adds Cloud Rebuild to reinstall OS and drivers
items.content:
Microsoft has introduced Cloud Rebuild, a recovery feature that wipes and reinstalls Windows 11 while pulling fresh system drivers directly from Windows Update. Rolling out via optional preview update KB5127936 for Windows 11 25H2 and 26H2, the tool can retrieve a clean OS image even when the local installation refuses to boot.
According to VideoCardz, users can initiate a Cloud Rebuild through Settings > System > Recovery as “Rebuild PC” whenever the OS boots normally. When startup fails repeatedly, the machine drops into the Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE), where Cloud rebuild appears under the Troubleshoot menu. Unlike the existing Cloud download setting in the Reset menu, Microsoft states that Cloud Rebuild doesn't rely on an intact local Windows installation.
Initiating the process completely wipes the primary drive, erasing installed software, local files, and user accounts, with only cloud-synced data surviving. For machines being repurposed or sold, a sanitize mode provides a secure disk erase. Moreover, system administrators can trigger rebuilds remotely using the Recovery CSP.
Executing the process requires a functioning WinRE partition and active network connectivity via Wi-Fi or Ethernet using pre-installed manufacturer drivers. WinRE can now reuse saved Wi-Fi profiles from Windows, though Microsoft notes the rebuild will fail if a system's drivers aren't published on Windows Update.
KitGuru says: Having an official recovery option that pulls fresh drivers alongside a clean image could save plenty of headaches when troubleshooting broken boots. Do you keep a dedicated Windows installer USB around, or will you start to rely on Cloud Rebuild from now on?

Phantom Blade Zero launches to over 800,000 concurrent players on Steam alone
items.content:
After almost a decade in development, S-GAME’s long-awaited Phantom Blade Zero has finally arrived. Already a success critically, the action-focused RPG has proven to be a commercial juggernaut – having officially landed on Steam with a concurrent player count of over 800K in total.
Officially released this past Thursday, S-GAME’s Phantom Blade Zero is off to an excellent start so far, with the PC / PS5 exclusive arriving to an aggregate review score of 89%. Said critic scores, alongside a substantial amount of pre-launch excitement, appears to have led to an explosive launch for the game, with Phantom Blade Zero peaking at over 800,000 concurrent players on Steam alone (hitting 833K on Sunday).
This puts Phantom Blade Zero as one of the most-played games of all time on the platform, with its peak CCU landing at no. 14 on Steam’s all-time list – nestled in between Battlefield 6 (747K) and Baldur’s Gate 3 (875K).
While we of course do not have any public data for how the game is performing on PS5, Phantom Blade Zero is currently sitting at an average score of 4.71 stars across its 15,000+ reviews on the platform (compared to Steam’s 78,000 ratings).
Prior to the title’s release, the team at S-GAME revealed that Phantom Blade Zero had amassed more than 3 million wishlists. While we have yet to learn just how many copies have been sold since its launch on the 29th of October, it is safe to say that with over 800K concurrent players on Steam alone, Phantom Blade Zero is already easily a 1 million+ seller.

items.title: OpenMouse expands beyond gaming mice with keyboard support
items.content:
OpenMouse, the open-source alternative to software suites like Logitech G Hub, Razer Synapse and SteelSeries GG, has expanded beyond gaming mice with new keyboard support. The latest beta release adds compatibility for keyboards from Logitech, Razer, SteelSeries and Wooting, allowing users to manage settings without relying on each manufacturer's software package.
As spotted by TechPowerUp, the OpenMouse project originally launched as a community-driven alternative to proprietary mouse configuration tools and now supports more than 260 mice across dozens of brands. With the latest beta, OpenMouse is beginning to extend the same approach to gaming keyboards, bringing support for features such as adjustable actuation, Rapid Trigger, SOCD, per-key RGB lighting and profile management, depending on the keyboard model.
Image credit: TechPowerUp
Keyboard support remains a work in progress, however. According to reports, some models are already functioning correctly, while others still exhibit issues. For example, a Wooting 80HE reportedly connected successfully during testing but was unable to correctly load keymaps or apply configuration changes. Key remapping functionality also appears to be absent from the current beta release.
OpenMouse's developers are continuing to expand compatibility and are encouraging users to participate in testing. If the project reaches its goals, it could eventually offer a single configuration tool for peripherals from multiple manufacturers, reducing the need to install separate software suites for each device.
KitGuru says: Would you replace G Hub, Synapse or SteelSeries GG with a single open-source alternative?

Assassin’s Creed Valhalla celebrates 40 million players with NG+ mode and more
items.content:
Despite many of their modern entries being somewhat by-the-numbers, Ubisoft’s Assassin’s Creed franchise continues to be a massive part of the publisher’s portfolio. As part of the company’s recent Fall 2026 franchise update, the team at Ubisoft announced that 2020’s Assassin’s Creed Valhalla is set to receive a surprise update in celebration of the game’s latest milestone – having officially surpassed 40 million total players.
During the team’s latest franchise update (where-in they confirmed that there are currently no AC remakes in the works), Ubisoft revealed that one of the franchise’s most maligned releases – Assassin’s Creed Valhalla – continues to attract millions of new players, writing:
“Assassin's Creed Valhalla recently surpassed 40 million players and, to celebrate, we're bringing one of the community's most requested features: the (very, very, very) long-awaited New Game+, arriving November 5.”
Of course, 40 million players does not equate to 40 million copies sold, especially as Valhalla has been playable across a multitude of services including but not limited to PlayStation Plus and the publisher’s own Ubisoft+ subscription platform.
Still, for a game which is deemed by many to be one of Assassin’s Creed’s weakest entries (mired by a bloat of content and minimal opportunities to roleplay as an actual assassin), 40 million players is a massive figure.
Assuming Valhalla’s 100+ hour experience wasn’t enough for you, the new game+ mode introduces a suite of additions, including:
New runes
A stash system
New rewards / cosmetics
Mithril – “a new resource to upgrade Divine Gear and strengthen runes”
Additionally, the team announced that the upcoming patch will bring with it “current-generation console updates”. Given the fact that Valhalla already has a native current-gen release, it will be interesting to see what exactly is added. Official PS5 Pro support perhaps? We won’t have to wait long to find out.

Mark's enthusiasm for computers dampened at an early age by the rubber-keyed Sinclair Spectrum 48K and feelings of Commodore 64 envy. However, in the mid-80s, hope in a digital future was rekindled by the purchase of an Atari 520 STe. Since that time Mark has used a multitude of computers for fun and professional endeavors. He often owned both Macs and PCs but went cold on the former after OS9 was killed off, and warmed to the latter with the introduction of Windows XP.

Early work years were spent in artwork and reprographics but in the late noughties, Mark started to blog about computers, Taiwanese food culture, and guitar design. This activity led to a full-time position writing about breaking PC tech news for HEXUS, for the best part of a decade. When HEXUS was abruptly closed, Mark helped with the foundation of Club386, before finding a new home at Tom's Hardware.

When not wearing through the keycap legends on his PC keyboards, Mark can be found wandering the computer malls of Taiwan's neon-lit conurbations and enjoying local and international cuisine.

items.title: Gears of War: E-Day has reportedly sold 400,000 copies despite half a Billion Dollars budget
items.content:
Initially set to launch across PC, Xbox and PlayStation, The Coalition’s Gears of War: E-Day was seemingly pivoted to becoming an Xbox console exclusive at the last-minute in an effort to boost Microsoft’s console output. Whether this will prove to have been a smart move in the long-term remains to be seen, but according to insiders, Gears of War E-Day has been off to a slow start – with the title reportedly having sold less than half-a-million units so far (despite costing $500 million to develop).
As expected from Microsoft, the console maker has not shared any official data regarding the early performance of their most-recent exclusive: Gears of War: E-Day. That said, multiple insiders have since come out to offer some preliminary figures, with The Verge’s Tom Warren claiming: “One source tells me that more than 400,000 copies of the game have been sold across Xbox and Steam.”
While 400K units sold is certainly nothing to sniff as (especially as the game released less than a month ago and was available day-one on Xbox Game Pass), E-Day will likely need to sell well over 5 million copies in order to break-even.
This is due to the fact that according to multiple sources – including known insider Jason Schreier – the total budget for Gears of War: E-Day landed at around $500 million. Considering the fact that the best-selling entry of all time (Gears 2) is said to have sold fewer than 7 million units, it begs the question as to whether E-Day will be able to make its money back at all.
Of course, being a console exclusive, E-Day is in some ways intended as an Xbox-seller more so than a title designed to push as many units as possible. Still, with its half a Billion budget and fewer than 500,000 copies sold so far, it will be interesting to see whether Microsoft deems their strategy of making the game exclusive as having been a success or not.

items.title: Sony’s Bend Studio will reportedly release its next game in 2027
items.content:
Since the arrival of their last game all the way back in 2019, we’ve heard very little from Sony’s Bend Studio, with the most recent reports claiming that the team were at one point working on a live-service title which was ultimately cancelled – leading to nearly a 3rd of the studio’s workforce being laid off. Despite this, the team appear to have been working hard on another new project, with reports claiming that Sony Bend’s next title is set to be announced and released in 2027.
As reported by the publication mp1st, despite having their previous live-service game cancelled by Sony, the Days Gone team at Bend Studio are currently in the advanced stages of development on an entirely new project.
Though early details remain light, according to the report, Sony Bend is currently planning to unveil their new game some time in 2027. That’s not all however, with the publication claiming that this title is also scheduled to launch next year, owing to it being “much further along in development” than some might expect.
That said, little else is known about the title as of right now, with the only other ‘confirmed’ details being the fact that it will be an entirely new IP which utilises a 3rd-person perspective, alongside some form of co-op functionality (though the extent of this remains unknown).
Though Days Gone failed to match the highs of other first-party PlayStation offerings critically, the open-world shooter did manage to be a commercial success in the long-run, with the infamous Insomniac Games leak revealing that the title had reached nearly 7.5 million copies sold as of early 2022.
While leaked details on the live-service ‘Project Mirror Pond’ did show some promise, it is encouraging to see that its cancellation appears to have not set the team back too much. Still, with Days Gone nearing 8 years old, it is high time we got to see something new from the studio.

Epomaker launches affordable EM3 tri-mode gaming mouse with charging dock
items.content:
Epomaker has announced the EM3, a new lightweight wireless gaming mouse featuring a carbon fibre-reinforced shell and a bundled magnetic charging dock. Despite those premium touches, the mouse arrives with an affordable $35.99 price tag.
Weighing around 56g, the EM3 is aimed at gamers looking for a lightweight mouse without venturing into enthusiast-level pricing territory. The mouse uses a PAW3315 optical sensor with support for up to 16,000 DPI and offers tri-mode connectivity via 2.4GHz wireless, Bluetooth and USB. Epomaker says the shape has been designed for small to medium-sized hands, particularly for claw-grip users.
Power comes from a 600mAh battery, which Epomaker rates for up to 55 hours of use on a full charge. The EM3 also ships with a magnetic charging dock that uses contact pins to recharge the mouse when docked. Alongside charging duties, the dock incorporates RGB lighting controls through a dedicated hardware button.
Users can customise settings through Epomaker's Driver 3.0 software or the browser-based Epomaker Hub utility. The software supports features such as button remapping, macro creation and DPI adjustment, allowing users to tailor the mouse to their own preferences.
The Epomaker EM3 is available in black, silver and pink, with pricing set at $35.99.

items.content: The original Fable checked all of the boxes of a good fairy tale: a classic good-versus-evil tale set in a high-fantasy version of Fake Britain. You played as a hero (literally, the “Hero of Oakvale”) fighting against a guy who considered burning down villages his idea of a good time. Fable’s big innovation lay in its morality system: Depending on your actions, the hero’s appearance would change (ex: you’d grow devil horns if you were evil), as would the way the citizens of Albion would react to him. Just like the main characters of stories like Jack and the Beanstalk, Little Red Riding Hood, and other quintessential fairy tales, you were consigned to live with the consequences of your actions — good or bad.

items.content: Even more significant than the quantity of Star Trek that Stewart made was the quality. Kirk is in many ways a classic pulp action hero. He faces conflicts head on, never afraid to throw a punch or flirt with a sexy alien. Picard represents a different form of masculinity, valuing compassion, knowledge, and communication above all else. He is the endlessly patient father figure for his crew, and for the next generation of Star Trek viewers, presiding over one of the most beautiful visions of what the future could look like. It’s that connection that has left fans in mourning following his death on Thursday at the age of 86.

Mark's enthusiasm for computers dampened at an early age by the rubber-keyed Sinclair Spectrum 48K and feelings of Commodore 64 envy. However, in the mid-80s, hope in a digital future was rekindled by the purchase of an Atari 520 STe. Since that time Mark has used a multitude of computers for fun and professional endeavors. He often owned both Macs and PCs but went cold on the former after OS9 was killed off, and warmed to the latter with the introduction of Windows XP.

Early work years were spent in artwork and reprographics but in the late noughties, Mark started to blog about computers, Taiwanese food culture, and guitar design. This activity led to a full-time position writing about breaking PC tech news for HEXUS, for the best part of a decade. When HEXUS was abruptly closed, Mark helped with the foundation of Club386, before finding a new home at Tom's Hardware.

When not wearing through the keycap legends on his PC keyboards, Mark can be found wandering the computer malls of Taiwan's neon-lit conurbations and enjoying local and international cuisine.

items.title: Let’s Game Now raises ₹30 Crore to build Indian Super Gaming League
items.content:
The capital will support the development of the Indian Super Gaming League (ISGL), a franchise-based gaming and entertainment property. (Photo credit: Inc 42)
Bengaluru-based esports company Let’s Game Now has raised ₹30 crore to accelerate the development of the Indian Super Gaming League (ISGL), a franchise-based gaming and entertainment property.
The investment round was led by industrialist Anand Mahindra and Bestvantage Investments, with participation from an undisclosed UAE-based family office, according to Inc42. The company has not disclosed its valuation, the equity stake involved or the individual contributions of the investors.
The funding will support the development of ISGL, which aims to bring competitive gaming, sports and entertainment together through a structured franchise model.
Building a franchise-based esports league
ISGL is central to Let’s Game Now’s expansion plans. The proposed league is designed around teams and recurring competitions, moving beyond standalone tournaments and brand-led gaming events.
The league was announced with eight teams associated with established sporting properties: Mumbai City FC, FC Goa, Chennaiyin FC, Kerala Blasters FC, Inter Kashi, Puneri Paltan, Bangalore Bhargavas and Andhra Agneyas.
Its format spans five games: chess, EA Sports FC 26, Call of Duty: Mobile, FAU-G and Cricket 26. The competition is designed to use city-based qualifiers as a route for players to enter the league.
The funding is expected to help Let’s Game Now advance the league's development. However, the company has not announced a detailed timeline for its next stage or disclosed the proposed franchise economics.
Anand Mahindra’s investment in esports
Mahindra’s participation connects the venture with an investor who has previously been involved in building professional sports leagues in India, including the Pro Kabaddi League and the Global Chess League.
The investment also comes as esports companies explore business models built around franchises, sponsorships, broadcasting and organised competitions.
For ISGL, the challenge will be to attract franchise owners and commercial partners while building a consistent audience across games and seasons.
Let’s Game Now’s existing gaming network
Founded in 2018 by Santanu Basu, Let’s Game Now operates an esports platform that connects brands with gaming communities. Its services include online competitions, offline events, and live broadcasting across South Asia and Southeast Asia.
The company claims to have a community of more than 1.4 million members and to have organised over 2,000 events across more than 18 countries. It also says it works with over 30 clients.
This existing network could provide a base for acquiring participants and audiences for ISGL. The company will, however, need to convert that reach into sustained viewership and recurring commercial revenue.
The commercial test for ISGL
India's large gaming audience offers an opportunity for organised esports properties, but building a franchise-based league requires more than a large player base.
ISGL will need to establish a sustainable model for franchise participation, sponsorships, media partnerships and audience engagement. The costs of production, marketing and league operations will also have to be supported by recurring revenue.
The ₹30 crore investment gives Let’s Game Now capital to develop the property. Its longer-term prospects will depend on whether it can turn the league into a commercially sustainable competition with consistent participation and viewership.

Mark's enthusiasm for computers dampened at an early age by the rubber-keyed Sinclair Spectrum 48K and feelings of Commodore 64 envy. However, in the mid-80s, hope in a digital future was rekindled by the purchase of an Atari 520 STe. Since that time Mark has used a multitude of computers for fun and professional endeavors. He often owned both Macs and PCs but went cold on the former after OS9 was killed off, and warmed to the latter with the introduction of Windows XP.

Early work years were spent in artwork and reprographics but in the late noughties, Mark started to blog about computers, Taiwanese food culture, and guitar design. This activity led to a full-time position writing about breaking PC tech news for HEXUS, for the best part of a decade. When HEXUS was abruptly closed, Mark helped with the foundation of Club386, before finding a new home at Tom's Hardware.

When not wearing through the keycap legends on his PC keyboards, Mark can be found wandering the computer malls of Taiwan's neon-lit conurbations and enjoying local and international cuisine.
