Summary
Chaotic new take on hockey out now on Xbox Series X|S.
Brutal fights, ridiculous takedowns and riveting action within a unique narrative.
How we imagined a game inspired by childhood hockey playing and storytelling.
What happens when five Finnish developers take the hockey they grew up playing on frozen ponds and turn it into a story about the greatest underground hockey player who ever lived?
When I think about my childhood, some of my best memories aren’t from school, holidays or birthday parties.
They’re from the ice.
Growing up in Finland, I spent enormous amounts of time on frozen outdoor rinks and ponds, playing hockey with friends. You didn’t need to organize it weeks in advance or check everyone’s calendar. You just went to the rink. Games happened. Friendships happened. Some of the people I met through hockey back then are still my friends today.
There was something special about those games. The rules could be flexible, teams could change, and somebody would inevitably try something ridiculous. That feeling became one of the starting points for Puckoff.
When we created Puckoff: Reloaded, we wanted to bring some of that feeling back. Many of the game’s rinks are frozen outdoor ponds inspired by the places where we grew up playing.
Then we asked ourselves a simple question: What if winning didn’t mean scoring more goals?
A Different Kind of Hockey
In most hockey games, you know what you’re supposed to do: Get the puck. Score goals. Win the game. In Puckoff: Reloaded, there are a few more options. You can score. Set up a teammate. Make the perfect pass. Or you can knock someone out.
And nobody in this world seems particularly bothered by that last option.
That’s the world we wanted to create: a story-driven hockey game where fighting isn’t a random side activity, but part of the sport and its strange underground culture. I’ve played a lot of the big hockey games over the years. They’re great at what they do, but I always found myself thinking: “Why can’t I just do that?”
You know the feeling. An opponent does something you don’t like, and you want to give them a little… extra attention. But the game tells you no. That’s when I realized one of the things I love about games. They let us experiment, cause chaos and do things we wouldn’t necessarily do in real life. So, I thought: what if a hockey game actually embraced that? That’s how Puckoff: Reloaded began.
In our version of hockey, scoring goals is still useful. It’s just not the only way to win.
We’re Not Just Making a Hockey Game
I’ve always loved storytelling, and for years I’ve had a particular dream: What would it be like if a big hockey game actually had a real story? Not just a career mode where you play a season and upgrade your player. I mean a proper story. Characters you care about. Mysteries. Rivalries. Friendships. A reason to wonder what happens next. That’s what we wanted Puckoff: Reloaded to be.
Between matches, the game uses a visual-novel-inspired presentation to tell a larger story. The hockey games aren’t disconnected challenges. They’re part of a journey. And that journey is about finding a legend.
The Search for Dominator
At the heart of Puckoff: Reloaded is a hockey legend named Dominator. He’s been playing underground hockey matches for decades, and nobody really knows how he’s managed to keep going for so long. What everyone does know is that he has never lost a game.
For the player character, Dominator isn’t just another hockey player. He’s the reason to keep playing. The dream is simple: find Dominator and eventually play alongside him. Getting there means meeting the people who inhabit this underground hockey world and proving you’re good enough to belong in it. Eventually, that leads to the Cage.
Welcome to the Cage
The biggest fights in Puckoff: Reloaded don’t happen in a traditional hockey arena. They happen underground.
The Cage is where some of the game’s most dangerous opponents are waiting. These boss matches are different from ordinary games: you’re not simply facing another team and trying to score more goals. You’re facing a character with their own identity, abilities and way of playing. And if you’re going to get closer to Dominator, you’ll have to get through them.
Our Dream is Bigger Than This Game
I’m proud of what our five-person team has created, but I also see Puckoff: Reloaded as the beginning of something. My dream has always been to make story-driven hockey games with the scope and production values of the big-budget games. I want hockey games where you remember the characters as much as the matches. Stories that make you care who wins. I want a game where you can spend an evening playing hockey with your friends, laughing when somebody gets knocked out—and then come back the next day because you genuinely want to know what happens to the characters.
We’re not a huge studio. We’re five people in Finland making the game we wanted to play. For me, that’s what Puckoff has always been about. It started with the frozen ponds where some of my best childhood memories were made. Now we’re taking those memories, adding a ridiculous amount of fighting, creating a hockey legend who hasn’t lost in decades, and turning the whole thing into a story.
We just have to find Dominator first.

items.title: Avatar Legends: The Fighting Game Enters the Avatar State
items.content:
The Avatar State Patch is available today for Avatar Legends: The Fighting Game on XBOX Series X|S, and it’s the biggest update the game has seen. It brings a fresh new look for the game’s menus and in-match displays, two totally reimagined fighters, Ranked Mode 2.0, quality-of-life upgrades for story, versus, and online play, plus balance changes for every character on the roster.
Since the game launched earlier this year with 12 characters from “Avatar: The Last Airbender” and “The Legend of Korra,” fighters have been putting their bending (or boomerangs) to the test, and our team has been watching closely. This patch is the result. It’s the game we envisioned from the beginning, and now it’s ready for you to play.
What’s in the Avatar State Patch:
A new look, everywhere. Menus, character select, stage select and the in-match interface have all been redesigned.
Two reimagined fighters. Avatar Aang and Nightmare Korra return with new art, new attacks and new super moves.
Every fighter rebalanced. From Aang to Zaheer, every character has been fine-tuned for fairer, more exciting matches.
More ways to play and learn. Story Mode+, Story difficulty settings, new tutorials and Combo Trials, Story stages in Versus, and more.
Reimagined Characters: Avatar Aang and Nightmare Korra
The two fighters at the heart of this patch are among the most powerful forms in the Avatar universe. Studio Art Director Giancarlo Montalbano, Art Director Santiago R. Villa, and Combat Director Young share how they brought them to life, and why they took the pair in opposite directions. “For Aang, his Avatar pose looks to elevate his presence in all ways, while for Korra it looks to diminish it. One is solemn and imposing while the other is languid and elusive.” Villa explains.
Avatar Aang
Avatar Aang’s character sheet, with his glowing Air Nomad tattoos idle pose, full turnaround and the lightning scar on his back.
In the Avatar State, Aang taps into the power of every Avatar who came before him. Young points to his final showdown with Fire Lord Ozai as the biggest touchstone, along with Avatar State moments across the series, from channeling Kyoshi on Avatar Day to facing the Sandbenders. While regular Aang is playful, Young describes this version as pure, overwhelming power, landing precise elemental attacks with the smallest movements. Villa adds that he’s the only fighter in the game lit from below, a deliberate choice to make him look mysterious and boss-like. Young’s favorite move is his signature special, Avatar’s Ascension, which lifts him into an air sphere packed with callbacks to the Ozai fight.
His new Level 4 super, his most powerful attack, brings in a special guest: Avatar Roku, straight out of the Winter Solstice two-parter. “Aang’s direct manifestations of prior Avatars ended up being something very unique to him,” says Young, “so we felt like we had to include it!”
Montalbano admits Avatar Aang was the trickier of the two, since his arm tattoos had to read correctly from every angle. Villa shares another hard call: Aang’s foot scar is missing, because with fighters switching sides, it would have been on the wrong foot half the time.
Nightmare Korra
Nightmare Korra’s character sheet. Her hunched idle pose, chains on both wrists, and menacingly glowing eyes set her apart from Korra.
Young explains that Nightmare Korra is the dark reflection that haunted Korra in “The Legend of Korra” episode Korra Alone, with her final fight against Zaheer at the end of Book 3 as another influence. “She’s a manifestation of that berserk state…alongside being a kind of spooky, ghost-like entity so we wanted to try and hit both of those angles pretty sharply. So you’ll see big contrasts between her slowly dragging her feet, then suddenly exploding into big chain swings or teleports.” Villa notes that she now wears chains on both wrists instead of one, a nod to how much weight they carry in her story.
Her visual effects are some of the wildest in the game. Montalbano highlights the mercury in her super moves and a victory pose that zooms through a fish-eye lens into her transformation into Vaatu, which he calls “very unique compared to a lot of other stuff in the game.” For Young, the standout is her Final Technique, Eternal Nightmare, a big team effort that looks just as striking when it misses as when it lands.
Young also shared a fun fact: early prototypes had her health constantly draining to represent mercury poisoning. It didn’t make for interesting play, so she simply starts with less health instead.
What’s new in battle
Battle Balance
There’s a lot to dig into, but here’s a closer look at two of the biggest shifts.
Azula’s Ambition’s Spark, her Focused Stance exclusive move, has vastly improved to allow much more variety in gameplay. It now automatically tracks much closer to your opponent’s position. Its detonation is a much greater hitbox and can also be flow cancelable.
Sokka’s sword special techniques, under certain circumstances using his Master Piandao support, can now directly cancel into a boomerang toss! Upon having at least 10 stacks of successful sword hits, Sokka permanently unlocks that ability for the rest of the match!
You can find the full patch notes on the Paramount Games site when the patch goes live.
Nightmare Korra: a new moveset to match
Nightmare Korra’s new look goes deeper than just that. Her kit has been rebuilt to match her haunting presence.
Avatar Aang: enter Roku!
Roku’s Inferno is Avatar Aang’s new Super Technique. Aang communicates with the spirit world, temporarily transforming him into Roku who engulfs the entire battlefield with a scorching flame.
Character Vote: You Pick the Next Fighter
If you pre-ordered Avatar Legends: The Fighting Game or upgraded to the Deluxe Edition, you get a say in who completes the Year 1 Pass, the set of five extra characters included with the Deluxe Edition. Iroh, Ty Lee, Lin Beifong and Bolin are confirmed, and the fifth spot is up to you. Standard Edition pre-orders get one vote, Deluxe Edition comes with an extra vote for Year 1 Pass. (For example: If you have two votes, you can either submit a new voting ranking, or duplicate the first vote). Upgrading to Deluxe (even without pre-order) will also entitle you to a vote. Voting runs for one month. Just look for the voting option on the main menu. The candidates are:
Tenzin
Kuvira
Amon
King Bumi
Asami Sato
The Avatar State Patch for Avatar Legends: The Fighting Game is available now on XBOX Series X|S. The Standard Edition is just $29.99, and the Deluxe Edition, which includes the Year 1 Pass, is $49.99. Thanks for fighting alongside us. The Avatar State Awaits.

items.title: Curse of Resthaven: Tips and Tricks to Unravel the Island’s Secrets
items.content:
Hi there! I’m Scott Christian, the studio director of Hilltop Studios here in Toronto, and the game director of Curse of Resthaven. We make games with a particular emphasis on strong characters, intricate storytelling, unique mechanics, and the occasional musical interlude.
Before making games, I spent fifteen years working as a composer and conductor here in Toronto, mainly in theatre. That background informs how we approach our games at Hilltop: character, timing, and a good dramatic reveal go a long way. Our debut, Lil’ Guardsman, was a comedic fantasy gate-guard simulator about a twelve-year-old put in charge of a castle gate, with the fate of the world in her hands.
For our follow-up, Curse of Resthaven, we decided to take a different turn into gothic horror, creeping dread, and a mystery that unfolds over a repeating six-day time loop. You play as Ambrose, the island’s newly appointed governor, tasked with restoring prosperity to the colony but he also has his own agenda: finding his missing niece, Amalia. The problem is that Resthaven is destroyed six days into his tenure… and Ambrose is sent back to the day of his arrival, the only one to remember the island’s fate.
Mashing up mechanics from narrative adventures, trading sims, deckbuilders, and roguelikes, Curse of Resthaven challenges you to investigate a town full of secrets, keep its economy running, and venture into the strange wilderness beyond its borders. You have six days to work with before disaster strikes and the island resets. Fortunately, you get to keep what you learn.
Solving the mystery is just the first step. You’ll soon discover there are three different timelines to explore, and only by reaching all three conclusions will you unlock the fourth, true ending.
Whether you’re stepping onto Resthaven for the first time or looking to make the most of your next loop, here are a few tips to help you get started.
A Few Simple Tips
Curse of Resthaven is a game about connecting the dots. Its systems feed into one another, and the best discoveries often come from combining information gathered in different ways. Here are a few things to keep in mind as you investigate the island.
Talk to everyone, and then talk to them again. Resthaven’s residents have their own motivations, grudges, and secrets. What someone tells you depends on what Ambrose already knows, what topics you bring up, and what has happened during the current loop. If a character isn’t being helpful, you may simply need to learn a little more before approaching them. Your journal can be counted on to let you know when to ask someone about something again.
Pay attention during interrogations. You can question characters about different topics to uncover clues, advance quests, and learn more about the island. Information gathered from one resident may unlock the topic needed to move the needle with another. If you’re stuck, revisit people you’ve spoken to and see whether they have a perspective on newly acquired topics or, better yet, can guide you in the right direction.
Don’t treat trading as a side activity. As governor, Ambrose is responsible for keeping Resthaven’s economy moving. Merchant ships bring goods to buy and sell, while the island’s businesses can be upgraded to produce useful resources. Money is only part of the equation: having the right resources is essential for pursuing opportunities elsewhere, including expeditions into the wilderness.
Experiment with your approach. Not every problem has an obvious solution, and not every promising lead will pay off immediately. Try different approaches, pursue unexpected conversations, and see where your investigations take you. Even a botched loop may teach you something useful for the next one.
Make the Most of the Time Loop
The six-day time loop is at the heart of Curse of Resthaven. Each loop begins with the island’s inhabitants returning to their usual routines, but Ambrose retains his knowledge and progression. That distinction is everything.
You aren’t expected to solve the entire mystery in one pass. Instead, each loop gives you another opportunity to apply what you’ve learned, approach old problems differently, and uncover information that was previously out of reach.
Knowledge is your most valuable resource. A character who refuses to cooperate on Day 1 might be much more forthcoming once you’ve discovered what motivates them. An apparently impossible obstacle might become straightforward once you know the right person to talk to or the right question to ask.
Plan your days around what you want to learn. There are more people to question, businesses to manage, and places to explore than you can necessarily get to in a single loop. Focus on the leads that seem most promising, and don’t worry if you have to leave something for next time.
Use each reset as an opportunity. When the island resets, you can take a different approach with the benefit of everything you’ve discovered. You don’t have to repeat the same actions just because you did them last time. If you already know where a particular lead is going, spend that time pursuing something new.
The goal isn’t simply to repeat the same six days until you get everything right. It’s to use what you learned last time to change what happens the next time.
Venture Beyond the Town
Beyond the safety of Resthaven’s fortified walls lies a much stranger version of the island. Expeditions take Ambrose into this wilderness through a card-based narrative system that blends roguelikes, deckbuilders, and choose-your-own-adventure games.
Each expedition draws encounters from a pool, meaning your journey can unfold differently from one attempt to the next. You’ll face decisions, discover strange events, and encounter opportunities that may not appear again on your next trip.
Expect the unexpected. Expeditions aren’t fixed sequences of events. The encounters you discover on one outing may be very different from those on another, so stay curious and be prepared to adapt.
Don’t assume you’ve seen everything. There are more encounters than you’ll experience in a single run. Returning to the wilderness on subsequent playthroughs can reveal entirely new stories and discoveries.
Remember that expeditions are part of the larger investigation. The wilderness isn’t separate from the mystery unfolding in town. Information and resources you gather can help you make progress elsewhere, so consider how an expedition might support your other goals.
Explore Every Corner Of Resthaven
It’s worth taking the time to look around. Beyond the main investigation, Resthaven contains optional discoveries, including collectible moth relics and other secrets tucked away throughout the town.
These discoveries reward players who aren’t in a rush. You can barely take a single step if you rely heavily on the handy town map + fast travel functionality, but you’ll certainly miss out on some optional, flavourful side content. Give yourself permission to wander a little. After all, in Resthaven you have nothing but time (in six-day intervals)!
And don’t be afraid to revisit familiar places. As you learn more about the colony and its inhabitants, locations and conversations that seemed unremarkable at first may take on new significance.
What To Do If You’re Stuck
Your journal is your best friend. Check your active leads for hints about what to pursue next. If you’ve exhausted all the possibilities in town, it may be time to head back out on expeditions and look for Amalia’s campsites. And your journal will probably tell you so!
Your journal has another trick up its sleeve, too. After the opening hours, you’ll unlock a timeline showing important events across the six-day loop and where they take place. If you’re stumped by a “???” on the timeline, it means something important is happening at that moment you haven’t discovered yet. To progress, you might just need to be in the right place at the right time.
The town map is another easy-to-miss resource. It shows which characters are accessible in each zone at any given time. Once you’ve spoken to a named NPC, their question mark becomes a portrait, making it much easier to track them down in subsequent loops. Still seeing a “?” in a zone? That might be a good place to start looking for someone new.
Finally, don’t underestimate the power of a little community gossip. Some leads require interrogation, but the answer might simply be to ask the townspeople about a particular topic. Resthaven is a small, tight-knit community, and information has a way of getting around.
We’ve designed the investigation around a trail of clues(We’ve classed them as bronze/silver/gold behind the scenes, but you won’t see these terms in-game.)
Bronze clues give you a little information and nudge you in the right direction, and many townspeople have them
Silver clues offer more specific details and bring you closer to the truth; fewer townspeople have them
Gold clues unambiguously reveal the next step in a lead. Only one or two townspeople have them
Follow the trail, and you shouldn’t be left out in the cold for long.
Don’t Worry About Seeing Everything the First Time
Curse of Resthaven features three branching timelines, each revealing different pieces of the larger mystery. You won’t necessarily encounter every quest or revelation during a single playthrough, and that’s intentional.
As you progress, you’ll uncover new information that changes how you understand the island and its people. Some discoveries will answer questions, while others will leave you with even more to investigate.
Once you’ve completed a timeline, New Game+ introduces Ambrose’s growing sense of déjà vu, allowing you to fast-track through content you’ve already experienced and focus on what’s different. You can spend less time retracing familiar steps and more time exploring new possibilities.
So don’t worry about finding every secret on your first visit. Pay attention, follow the leads that interest you, and let your growing knowledge guide you through the next loop.
Resthaven has a great many secrets. The trick is figuring out which ones to pursue, when to pursue them, and what to do with what you discover.
Six days remain. Good luck, Governor. You’ll need it.
Curse of Resthaven launches October 29 for XBOX Series X|S and XBOX on PC.

Take command of the cursed island colony of Resthaven after your niece disappears on the eve of catastrophe. Govern the town, interrogate suspicious locals, trade with visiting merchants, upgrade vital businesses, and decide who — or what — to trust as the island’s secrets begin to surface.
Beyond the safety of Resthaven’s walls, you will send card-driven expeditions into the island’s wilderness. Build a deck of resource and companion cards, choose who to bring, decide what to carry, and prepare for unpredictable encounters with eldritch horrors.
The cataclysm comes in just seven days. When destruction strikes, the island’s fading guardian intervenes, sending you back to the moment of your arrival with your memories and experience intact. Each loop offers new knowledge, permanent upgrades, and dangerous blessings from the island’s goddess — but every advantage may come with a cost.
Every loop reveals new truths about Resthaven, the forces seeking to control the island’s power, and your niece’s role in what is unfolding. Interrogate over 25 fully voiced characters, uncover their motives and secrets, and piece together a mystery shaped by mythology, history, and cosmic dread.
With multiple major narrative paths and randomized expeditions, every playthrough exposes different pieces of the puzzle. Only by mastering the town, surviving the island, and understanding the time loop can you hope to break the curse.

items.title: Queen’s Domain Releases Today! Some Beginner’s Pro Tips for Success
items.content:
Queen’s Domain is a retro-fantasy action RPG that strands you alone on the monster-infested isle of Neasied, available today on XBOX Series X|S. You’ll need wits as well as strength if you want to survive in this twisting, secretive world. Here’s a list of top tips for newly minted warriors, assembled by the Future Friends gang. Read on, if you don’t want to wind up as meat for the worms…
Your Sword is much more than just a weapon
If you think a sword can only be helpful for fighting monsters, think again! In Queen’s Domain, your sword is as much for traversing the world and platforming as it is for fighting. Practice ‘dashing’ with your holy sword, and soon you’ll be able to reach faraway places.
Each battle is a dance
Those who swing their weapons around wildly won’t last long on Neasied. If you are careless and don’t pay attention to the rhythms of your opponents, you’ll be defeated by even the most trifling of enemies. Watch carefully to learn their attack patterns, study the bestiary to learn their weaknesses, and make sure you use the right weapon for each encounter. Preparation is everything!
Curiosity pays
Queen’s Domain is designed to reward curiosity. Taking the path less trodden can lead you to hidden treasures, secret paths and much more. If you’re ever really stumped, here’s a top tip: the dead sometimes leave hints for the living…
Keep your eyes open
Enemies can come at you from any angle, and often when you least expect it. Make sure you equip your favourite throwable weapon when venturing out into the world and always look around you for potential threats around and above you. Blundering into open spaces is a quick way to a grisly end.
Not just you, your weapons Level Up too!
The more you practice with a weapon, the more powerful it will become! If you get stuck at an especially difficult place, try retracing your steps and leveling up your weapon of choice. Then you can save and return with a better chance at defeating the evils around you!
That’s all the wisdom we can offer you for now. This game is a labour of love from a small, passionate team, and we sincerely wish you the best of luck as you embark on this adventure.

items.title: Things That Go Beep in the Night: Agentic AI Joins the Search for Extraterrestrial Signals
items.content:
While science fiction lore tells us that humans will meet extraterrestrial life in the form of little green men, the detail that should raise hairs this Halloween is this: the search for extraterrestrial intelligence took a major leap forward with AI, and it increasingly focuses on AI agents built by humans listening for AI agents built by aliens.
Some scientists have suggested that extraterrestrial civilizations, if they exist, could be billions of years older than humanity. Such civilizations might have developed technologies far beyond humanity’s, including forms of AI.
Breakthrough Listen and the SETI Institute are bringing agentic AI into the daily search for extraterrestrial intelligence. At the Allen Telescope Array in Northern California, agents can now steer the instrument, enhance and correct incoming data, and apply AI models to the incoming stream — all from a single natural language request. The NVIDIA Holoscan platform processes the massive streams of sensor data, giving agents live data to act on.
The result is a faster, more adaptable search for potential signals from extraterrestrial life and technologies.
“As our new agentic observatories reach out into the universe, what they find may have much more in common with themselves than with the humans who created them,” said Andrew Siemion, Bernard M. Oliver chair for SETI at the SETI Institute and principal investigator of Breakthrough Listen. “But this isn’t something to fear. Rather, it’s a breakthrough in translation.”
Terabits a Second, Processed in Flight
Radio telescopes generate enormous volumes of data, creating a challenge for scientists who need to identify potentially interesting signals as observations unfold.
At the Allen Telescope Array, DAQIRI, a Holoscan platform library, enables the telescope to pull terabits per second of sensor data straight into GPU memory so observations are processed in flight rather than filling hard drives. CyberEther, a signal-processing framework developed at the SETI Institute, does the math using NVIDIA CUDA-X libraries including cuFFT and cuBLAS.
Nexus, a web-based observatory orchestrator, acts as the agent harness. It gives agents a single source of truth for instrument state, compute resources and pipelines and lets researchers monitor packet loss, read live spectrograms and rewrite signal-processing blocks — all by prompting in natural language. The system can handle 2.4 terabits per second on NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs, with inference running on premises, next to the instrument.
Put together, the system enables an agent to steer a telescope’s antennae, calibrate and focus the instrument for a clean signal, catch and fix data errors and plot the result. Agents compress what would take humans weeks or years into hours.
Science Fact, Not Fiction
The pipeline has already proven itself, achieving the first real-time AI detection of a pulsar — a rapidly spinning stellar remnant that pulses like a cosmic lighthouse — in the Crab Nebula.
Next, the team is evaluating open models including NVIDIA Nemotron for cases where data locality and turnaround matter most and for observatories that may someday run offline on the far side of the moon.
Learn more about NVIDIA AI for science.

items.title: Terrible Lizards: Movement Is Your Weapon
items.content:
Terrible Lizards, available now on XBOX Series X|S and Game Pass, is a first-person platforming game about escaping runaway dinosaur animatronics in an abandoned roadside attraction. That perspective was something we landed on pretty deliberately, through a process of both considering this particular game’s needs, as well as reviewing what we’ve loved about movement in other games.
When I think about the platforming games I’ve always enjoyed most, a lot of it comes down to rhythm. I like being able to move quickly, react to what’s coming, and string things together without constantly stopping to line everything up.
Jumping off the Shoulders of Giants
You can see that reactive flow really clearly in older 2D platformers like Donkey Kong Country or the early Mario games. With a limited screen in front of you, you don’t always have much time to plan. You’re reacting, trusting the mechanics, and finding a rhythm as you move through the level. That’s what I wanted to bring into Terrible Lizards, and the first-person perspective is a big part of bringing that satisfying, rhythmic, reactive gameplay to a 3D platformer.
Games like Mirror’s Edge and Dying Light are the obvious first-person platforming reference points, but we actually wanted Terrible Lizards to feel a little different moment to moment. We were chasing the tighter, more immediate game feel you get from games like Titanfall, Call of Duty, and Overwatch, where simply moving, jumping, and changing direction feels responsive and satisfying. You do see that kind of feel in first-person platforming games like Neon White, and that was closer to the balance we wanted: strong platforming mechanics built on top of controls that already feel good before you even start chaining moves together.
Floaty Empowerment
The controls needed to feel tight and immediate, but we also ended up giving the player a little bit of floatiness in the air. That mostly came from our aerial control system. Once you jump, you have the ability to adjust your trajectory before you land, and that became one of the most important pieces of the movement system.
For someone who isn’t especially confident with first-person platforming, it gives you room to correct yourself. If you jump too far, you can pull back. If you drift left or right, you can make a small adjustment. You have a little extra time to understand where you’re going and make the landing. At the same time, someone who gets really comfortable with the system can exploit that same freedom. They can make harder jumps, move through sections more efficiently, find faster routes, and occasionally bypass parts of a platforming sequence entirely.
That gave us something we were really happy with: a low skill floor, but a high skill ceiling. You don’t have to be amazing at platformers to play the game, but there’s a noticeably different way of moving through it once everything starts clicking. You can absolutely slow down, explore, look for collectibles, and work your way through the environments methodically. But once you understand the movement and start chaining together jumps, slides, wall runs, clambers, ledges, and swings without really thinking about each individual input, there’s a flow state to it that I find really satisfying.
No Fight, All Flight
We also made a very deliberate decision not to give the player weapons or other means to fight back. Your movement is really your main way of dealing with danger. When one of the creatures comes after you, the answer isn’t to turn around and shoot it. You have to move, and that made the monsters a natural way to test everything the player has been learning.
Sometimes that’s a direct chase. Sometimes a creature causes the environment around you to start collapsing and you have to survive. Other times you’re dropped into a more open arena where the monster is loose in the space with you and you have to complete objectives or figure out how to escape. Those moments let us use the same core movement mechanics in different ways without turning every encounter into the same kind of chase.
Between those moments, the game has more traditional platforming, exploration, environmental puzzles, and larger caverns where figuring out how to move through the space is part of the challenge. Then we can tighten things back down and put the player under pressure again. That variety was important to us. We didn’t want the whole game to be six hours of constant sprinting, and we also didn’t want movement to feel like something that only mattered in designated platforming sections.
It’s really the foundation of how you interact with the game. The story, collectibles, exploration, hunt arenas, and New Game Plus content all sit around that, but the movement is what everything keeps coming back to. Once players get comfortable with it, the hope is that they stop thinking about every individual mechanic and just start moving through the world naturally. That’s when the game shines, and obviously when something is chasing you, that familiarity with the movement starts to matter a lot more.
Terrible Lizards is available now on XBOX Series X|S and XBOX Game Pass.

Something is very wrong at Dalton’s Dinos, the once must-see Route 66 roadside attraction baking under the New Mexico sun. The staff have vanished, but a mysterious voice on the telephone you find in the attraction begs you for help to find a missing child.
You’d leave… if your car hadn’t died miles from anywhere. It’s 1992. No cell phones. No rideshares. No help coming, and you’ll soon find that you are not alone inside the attraction.
You’ll encounter monstrous creatures that will hunt, chase, and torment you. Take a moment to catch your breath, it may be your last.
RUN. CLIMB. SURVIVE.
Terrible Lizards blends horror with first‑person parkour, creating a relentless chase experience that feels intuitive to learn and has a lot to master.
You’ll be hunted by creatures that stalk the abandoned dino depot. They shamble and charge toward you, forcing you to run, jump, climb, wall run, bounce, and slide to survive. There are no weapons except your wits.

items.title: The Journey of Crimson Desert Continues with Charting the Unknown
items.content:
Summary
Crimson Desert Enhanced: Charting the Unknown will be available on October 29, 2026 for XBOX Series X/S, XBOX on PC, with XBOX Play Anywhere support.
Charting the Unknown adds new storylines, ocean exploration, romance, stronghold management, boss rushes, and more.
XBOX players can try Crimson Desert Enhanced with a 5-hour Free Trial from October 29, 2026 through January 7, 2027.
Since its launch in March, the world of Crimson Desert — where Kliff and the Greymanes fight to rebuild what they lost — has grown with each update. Alongside improvements, the game has received brand new content, including boss rematches, and new features shaped by players’ adventures and stories across Pywel.
In August, we released Patch Version 2.00. The free update added new story moments and expanded voice-over and language support. Together with all the post-launch updates up to that date, the update came out as Crimson Desert Enhanced.
Lastly, with the launch of Charting the Unknown on October 29, Pywel is growing once again with even more adventures. The DLC brings new journeys across land and, for the first time, at sea, along with new ways to enrich your life in Pywel. Charting the Unknown is available now on XBOX Series X|S.
We want to thank all our Greymanes out there for the incredible support they have shown for Crimson Desert since launch. Your love for the game has brought us this far, and we are excited for you to experience what the DLC has to offer.
Now, let’s take a look at what awaits you in Charting the Unknown.
New Stories
Charting the Unknown introduces three new storylines, one each for Kliff, Oongka, and Damiane. With the fight for the Greymanes and Pywel behind them, each character sets out to forge their own path. Along the way, they will meet allies and threats both old and new, and chart their own course forward.
Exploring the Ocean
The DLC brings something many players have been asking for: ocean exploration. Dive into the sea and explore the underwater world, where you will discover ruins, treasure chests, and new creatures and mounts. You can also build your own ship and set sail across the Great Ocean of Pywel.
A Richer Life in Pywel
Charting the Unknown also deepens life in the world. Kliff, Oongka, and Damiane can form deeper bonds with some of Pywel’s inhabitants. Interact with them to build trust and strengthen your relationship, which may eventually blossom into romance and even marriage.
An upgraded housing system now lets you build your house from the ground up. And from the layout of the interior to the placement of walls, windows, and other structural elements, you have more control than ever to design your home, sweet home. There’s more: select castles, once liberated, can become yours. This will allow you to decorate their courtyards and interiors with unique objects and furnishings, turning a hard-won stronghold into another place you can call your own.
Also, if you want to take a more active role in the strongholds you have liberated, you can lease certain facilities such as a restaurant or a smithy and run them yourself. Assign equipment and comrades, decide which goods to sell, and grow each location’s recognition.
Garden of Trials
For those who don’t always like life too peaceful, Charting the Unknown has new content for you. The Garden of Trials is a combat-focused challenge where you face the bosses you have met throughout your adventures in Pywel, one after another. So test your skills and mettle to see if you hold up against these formidable foes.
Whether you are a seasoned Greymane or just taking your first steps in Pywel, there is plenty to discover.
And if you have not set out on the journey yet, this is the perfect time to do so! Crimson Desert is offering a 5-hour free trial of the base game for XBOX players from October 29 through January 6, so take the opportunity to step into Pywel and reach beyond!

Discover an enhanced Crimson Desert, featuring new cutscenes and story moments, plus expanded voice-over and language support. ​

■ EXPLORE A WORLD OF DISCOVERY
Welcome to Pywel.
Here you'll find stretches of natural beauty and wilderness—from green plains and woods to arid deserts and rugged mountains. Between destinations, you will come across landmarks, ancient ruins, hidden treasures, and other points of interest that will draw your curisoity to wander.
Your journey will also inevitably take you skyward to the mysterious realm known as the Abyss, where a mystical imbalance endangering the world must be restored.
The world is yours to explore as you will and there are many paths for you to uncover.
Experience the continent's stories and tales through quests, encounters, challenges, and battles.
Roam the lands on various mounts from horses to even a dragon and mechs, and scale cliffsides and walls which you can leap from to glide.
■ FORGE YOUR OWN COMBAT
On the unforgiving battlefields of Crimson Desert, there is no single path to victory.​
Grow your arsenal of skills, weapons, and equipment—and decide how you want to use them.
Wield weapons like swords, spears, greatswords, axes, dual wields, various ranged weapons, and more, and unleash powerful abilities and elemental enhancements through lethal combinations.
With every strike and move, forge your own way in a world where a split second can decide your fate in fast-paced, visceral battles.
From ruthless warriors to fearsome beasts, there are those in Pywel who will seek your downfall. Encounter a diverse array of challenging enemies and bosses in brutal one-on-one duels, large-scale battle clashes, and quick skirmishes, and prevail against the threats that stand in your way.
■ LIFE IN PYWEL
In Pywel, many of the smaller moments also shape your journey and make up your day-to-day life.
Gather resources, cook, fish, hunt, and partake in the other various activities of Pywel for stat replenishment, making your equipment stronger, and more.
Along the way, enjoy some leisure time by playing minigames with the locals.
And shaping your daily life also extends to customization. Adjust hairstyles, tattoos, outfits, and more using dyes you brew or pick up along your journey.

items.title: METRO Redux Next-Gen Update Out Now for XBOX Series X|S
items.content:
The METRO Redux Next-Gen Update is out now on XBOX Series X|S consoles. Right now, you can experience both METRO 2033 & Last Light Redux with an unprecedented degree of immersion, thanks to performance improvements, enhanced visuals, and control upgrades that combine to take full advantage of the latest XBOX hardware.
First, the Next-Gen Update transforms the experience of playing both games through a series of major performance improvements. Once you’ve downloaded and applied the free update, you’ll be able to experience both titles in either true 4K resolution at 60fps or upscaled 4K at an even smoother 120fps. 4A TSR Upscaling and Antialiasing support will give players an even sharper, high fidelity experience.
Additionally, XBOX Ally and Ally X owners can look forward to full support and optimisation, plus the addition of XBOX Play Anywhere means fand and newcomers alike can truly experience the immersive world of METRO wherever they are.
As significant as these improvements are by themselves, there’s more to the update’s visual overhaul than enhanced framerates and sharper detailing. Alongside these core performance upgrades, the update dramatically modernises both titles with the introduction of more detailed textures, a refined lighting and shadow system that impacts every corridor and corner of each world, richer environmental detail, and enhanced animation fidelity.
Beyond these visual upgrades, the developers at 4A Games have also deepened the immersive quality of both titles by taking advantage of the latest XBOX controller hardware. With the Next-Gen Update, METRO players will experience full support for the XBOX controller’s Impulse Triggers, ratcheting up the tension through tactile feedback. METRO’s apocalyptic worlds don’t just look better than ever before, they feel better to explore too.
Although the update improves the core gameplay and visual experiences of both METRO 2033 and METRO Last Light, the 4A team has tuned each change carefully to authentically preserve the look and feel of the original games. The METRO universe has earned a passionate following over the last 16 years, and the new update’s been designed to respect the community’s deep affection for the worlds they already know.
If you’re a METRO veteran the Next-Gen Update gives you the chance to experience familiar worlds with fresh eyes, and a tenser, richer atmosphere throughout. Meanwhile, the update gives newcomers the perfect opportunity to lose themselves in a modern refresh of the series ahead of METRO 2039’s launch on February 4, 2027.
More than 50 million players have explored the grim, haunting worlds of the METRO series since the first game launched in 2010. Whether you’ve been with the series since the very beginning, or you’re feeling ready to take your first fearful steps through Moscow’s Metro, there’s never been a better time to lose yourself in 4A Game’s acclaimed atmospheric storytelling and experience the iconic, intense stealth-action gameplay of the METRO universe.

In 2013 the world was devastated by an apocalyptic event, annihilating almost all mankind and turning the earth’s surface into a poisonous wasteland. A handful of survivors took refuge in the depths of the Moscow underground, and human civilization entered a new Dark Age.
The year is 2033. An entire generation has been born and raised underground, and their besieged Metro Station-Cities struggle for survival, with each other, and the mutant horrors that await outside. You are Artyom, born in the last days before the fire, but raised underground. Having never ventured beyond the city limits, one fateful event sparks a desperate mission to the heart of the Metro system, to warn the remnants of mankind of a terrible impending threat. But will they even listen? Rather than stand united, the factions of the Metro are locked in a struggle for the ultimate power, a doomsday device from the military vaults of D6. A civil war is stirring that could wipe humanity from the face of the earth forever.
Including the epic single-player campaigns of both Metro 2033 and Metro: Last Light, Metro Redux takes you on a journey from the forgotten catacombs beneath the subway to the desolate wastelands above, where your actions will determine the fate of mankind.

Based on the internationally bestselling novel series by Dmitry Glukhovsky.

items.title: Weave Your Own Fate: Titan Quest II Is Now Available for Pre-Order on XBOX Series X|S
items.content:
Summary
Titan Quest II launches on XBOX Series X|S on January 19, 2027, and is available for pre-order starting today.
Players combine two of six Masteries into a hybrid class that perfectly matches their playstyle.
Both the Standard Edition ($59.99) and the Ultimate Edition ($79.99) include the Cosmic Turtle Companion and 96 hours of early access.
High above the clouds, the gods of Olympus watch in silence – for once, even they are powerless against what is coming. The fate of the world now rests in mortal hands. Your hands. But do you have what it takes to face a goddess? The THQ Nordic and Grimlore Games teams are thrilled to announce that Titan Quest II launches on XBOX Series X|S on January 19, 2027. And starting today, you can pre-order the game on XBOX.
Titan Quest II is the successor to the beloved original Titan Quest: an action RPG set in a reimagined ancient Greece, where you set out to stop Nemesis, the Goddess of Retribution, from corrupting the Threads of Fate. Since the game entered Early Access on PC in August 2025, we’ve worked hand in hand with our community. We read the feedback, ran the numbers, and added new regions, new Masteries, new enemies and bosses, crafting, multiplayer, tons of loot, and much more along the way. With the full release, the story reaches its conclusion, and the complete journey comes to XBOX.
So, what makes Titan Quest II stand out in a genre full of great action RPGs? It starts with the heart of the series: the Mastery system. Instead of locking yourself into a fixed class at the start of your adventure, you pick two Masteries and combine them into a hybrid class of your own. Titan Quest II launches with six Masteries – Earth, Storm, Warfare, Rogue, Forge, and Spirit – and each of them can be freely paired with any other. That’s 15 distinct combinations before you’ve even looked at your gear.
Earth commands fire and stone for devastating area damage. Storm calls down lightning and frost to control the battlefield. Warfare is all about raw physical might, while Rogue strikes from the shadows with poison and piercing blades. Forge, inspired by Hephaistos himself, reinforces your weapons and armor in the middle of a fight and deploys blade traps, sentry turrets, and ferociously fighting automatons. And Spirit lets you summon the dead and draw on your hero’s life force to fuel otherworldly spells. Want to set up blade traps crackling with lightning? Pair Forge with Storm. Rather send the dead ahead while you strike from the shadows? Spirit and Rogue have you covered.
And the customization doesn’t stop at the pairing. Every skill can be shaped with modifiers that do far more than add a few percent of damage – some change how a skill behaves entirely, like turning a sweeping strike into a channeled whirlwind. Attribute points in Might, Agility, Vigor, and Knowledge let you fine-tune your hero even further, and if you ever want to rethink your build from scratch, you can respec at any time (the gods charge a little gold for it, of course).
Did we mention that every hero can use whatever weapons and equipment they prefer? You can wear full plate armor while wielding a frost magic staff, or charge into battle clad in leather while swinging a two-handed axe. And an archer dressed in fine linen works perfectly well with any Mastery. The choice is truly yours.
The second thing that sets Titan Quest II apart is how it plays. Combat is deliberate rather than frantic. Enemies fight in factions and combine their abilities, so reading the battlefield, dodging at the right moment, and smart positioning matter just as much as raw damage. Even your health potions encourage you to stay in the fight: they refill as you deal damage to your enemies. IGN Germany summed up the Early Access version as “the ARPG for everyone who finds Diablo too hectic” – and we’ll happily take that. With Rituals, you also decide for yourself how hard the gods should test you, adjusting the challenge freely to your liking.
Loot matters, too. Items aren’t just bigger numbers; they serve a real purpose for your build, with plenty of equipment options for every class. Socket Charms and Relics into your gear, and use crafting to reroll, add, or upgrade affixes until every piece is exactly what your build needs.
All of this takes place in a beautiful, handcrafted world rooted in Greek myth. Venture across sun-drenched coasts, the Arkadian Plains, the untamed Wild Lands, and even Mount Olympus itself. Discover dark dungeons, uncover hidden groves where legendary monsters lurk, and stumble upon World Quests you can complete simply by finding them. Along the way, you’ll face creatures straight out of legend, from centaurs and gryphons to cyclopes, all set to a soundtrack that blends traditional Greek music with orchestral grandeur. And if you’d rather not take on Nemesis alone, you can explore Greece together with friends in cooperative multiplayer.
Ready to answer the call? Pre-orders for Titan Quest II open today, October 28, on XBOX Series X|S, with two editions to choose from:
Titan Quest II Standard Edition – $59.99 / €59.99: Includes the Cosmic Turtle Companion as a pre-order bonus and 96 hours of early access. Owners of the original Titan Quest on XBOX also receive a 10% loyalty discount.
Titan Quest II Ultimate Edition – $79.99 / €79.99: Includes the Cosmic Turtle Companion as a pre-order bonus and 96 hours of early access, plus the original Titan Quest and its expansions Ragnarök and Atlantis – playable immediately upon pre-order.
With 96 hours of early access, you can begin your journey as early as January 15, 2027. And if you go for the Ultimate Edition, the original Titan Quest and both expansions are yours right away – the perfect way to warm up for the sequel (or to finally find out what happened in Atlantis).
Titan Quest II launches on XBOX Series X|S on January 19, 2027. Pre-order now – the gods are counting on you!

Return to the classic mythology-inspired setting of Titan Quest and go toe-to-toe with legendary monsters as you journey across a fantastical reimagining of ancient Greece.
Nemesis, Goddess of Retribution, is out of control. She is corrupting the Threads of Fate and condemning all those who oppose her to eternal punishment – including you. Take up your weapon, fight alongside gods, and change fate itself in order to stop Nemesis, free those she’s punished, and weave your own epic tale.
From the creators of SpellForce 3 comes a handcrafted action RPG for a new generation of mythical heroes.
A World of Myth and Monsters
Set out on an adventure worthy of myth that takes you from picturesque beaches, to serene Greek temples, to places where no mortal has ever ventured, including the mysterious realm of the Moirai themselves.
Battle classic creatures from Greek myth and the original Titan Quest, including Ichthians, Centaurs, Satyrs, Harpies, Sirens, Gryphons, and many, many more.
Exploration-Focused Campaign
Pay close attention to your surroundings! The world is full of mysteries and secrets to discover. Legendary monsters lurk in hidden groves, and you never know when you will end up face-to-face with a god.
Visit memorable towns full of life and intrigue. The conversations you engage in and the items you find along your journey can lead to surprising discoveries, or they might just hold the key to stopping Nemesis. This is your adventure.
A Challenge Fit for a Hero
Heroic deeds require heroic effort. The enemies you face are far from defenseless – dodge and counter their attacks, then overwhelm them with a well-timed flurry of blows.
Powerful rituals allow you to freely control the game’s difficulty, while deep character customization systems ensure that there’s always a good reason to replay.
Key Features:
Flexible character system: In Titan Quest 2, you are in control of you own fate. Customize your hero, then form your own class by combining two masteries. Build your character around the strengths and weakness of both masteries, exploring different combinations of skill modifiers, attributes, and items to create your own hybrid class and find your favorite playstyle. Grow your powers from those of a young mortal to a hero to rival the gods themselves!
Meaningful loot: Every item serves a function, and every character class has many options when it comes to finding the perfect equipment. Even the most common spear can be upgraded via affix crafting, and with the right ingredients, you may even forge it into a unique item spoken of only in legend!
Challenging action RPG combat: Enemies form factions and work together, combining their unique skills and abilities to keep you on your toes. Use the deep character build system and access every skill at your disposal to vanquish them in this unique action RPG experience.
A beautiful, handcrafted world rooted in Greek myth: Encounter stunning vistas and deep caverns, and traverse the world with your divine mount, Areion. Use the powers of the gods to uncover secret locations and explore lovingly designed levels full of verticality.
Online multiplayer: Join up with friends to take on the Goddess of Retribution. Like Jason and the Argonauts, sometimes you need a group of heroes for your journey.
Rich and immersive sound: An atmospheric soundtrack blends traditional Greek music with modern orchestral elements to create epic, memorable themes, drawing you into Titan Quest 2's unique world.

items.title: Phantom Blade Zero: How boss weapons transform combat and exploration
items.content:
Phantom Blade Zero blends influences from a variety of sources to create intense, fast-paced combat and a supernaturally infused Kungfupunk world. It draws on the tough, powerful bosses of Soulslikes, the quick, combo-focused combat of hack-and-slash games, the fascinating stories and characters of RPGs, and the unlockable exploration of search action games.
All those ideas come together to create something familiar and unexpected, reworking common action-RPG elements into beautiful, fast-paced battles across a strange, devastated world.
Mixing aggression and defense
Verify your age to view this content.
Verify your age to view this content.
While Phantom Blade Zero’s combat evokes games like Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice and Bloodborne, it takes a more hybrid approach, channeling Wuxia stories and kung-fu movies. You’re not just using R1 to dodge, holding L1 to block blows, or tapping L1 to parry them; you also need to press attack, using Square for basic attacks and Triangle for more powerful blows to create simple but effective combos and force your opponent to block and parry as well.
Verify your age to view this content.
Verify your age to view this content.
It’s all about managing a meter measuring your Sha-Chi. Blocking attacks depletes your Sha-Chi, and if it runs out, you can be staggered and left open to attack — but perfectly parrying, and dodging and landing blows knocks down your opponent’s Sha-Chi instead, letting you cut through their defenses.
You can quickly refill your Sha-Chi by pressing Left on the D-Pad to swap between your two equipped main weapons. The system pushes you to string attacks together from both weapons, or to swap as you end your strikes so you’re ready to start parrying.
Verify your age to view this content.
Verify your age to view this content.
As you land attacks, you also earn Sha-Chi Essence. When it’s fully charged, you can unleash a Power Surge attack with L2 that overpowers your opponent, interrupts their attacks, and deals massive damage. All those elements, combined with powerful Phantom Edge weapons that have specific but limited uses, work together to turn battles into a fluid dance that constantly moves between attack and defense. And thanks to haptic feedback in the DualSense controller, you feel those clashing blades, adding intensity that shows how powerful and lethal their blows can be.
Using the weapons of the enemy
One of the best parts of Phantom Blade Zero is the way it dishes out new weapons. Instead of finding swords in treasure chests or buying them from merchants, you claim most of your weapons from bosses you defeat. You get to see exactly how a weapon works as you defend against its unique capabilities, then try those capabilities yourself.
Verify your age to view this content.
Verify your age to view this content.
For instance, after you defeat the boss Hua, Deadly Betrothed, you can claim her Scarlet Wraithblade, which summons spider lilies on the ground as you complete combos that slow down enemies and let you control the battlefield.
The White Serpent and Crimson Viper are dual-wielded swords, and you can use each one’s separate combo, or mix them together for different effects that let you use one sword up close and send the other spinning in circles around you.
Each weapon offers its own fighting style, special combos, and status effects, like causing enemies to bleed for extra damage or allowing you to siphon their life. With so many varied combat options, you’ll constantly want to try different weapons and see how they exploit the weaknesses of the tough bosses you’ll face.
Uncovering the mysteries of the Wulin
Exploration is also a big part of the experience. The game is full of side quests and stories to chase down that flesh out the Wulin, the game’s world, and the characters you meet along the way.
Each area you visit is expansive, with lots of side paths and secrets to find. Often, you’ll come across areas you can’t reach yet, encouraging you to backtrack later after finding an essential item. Some paths are blocked by specific Phantom Edge weapons that you’ll earn from defeating bosses, making it possible to smash through a barrier or grapple up to a distant location.
Verify your age to view this content.
Verify your age to view this content.
Phantom Blade Zero ties its storytelling, exploration, and combat together by rewarding you for your curiosity. Exploring new areas will often advance old side quests and uncover new ones. Discovering Blue Memory Flowers scattered throughout the world gives you glimpses into the past that unlock the stories of the places you visit. Finding all the flowers for a given story also increases Soul’s health, making him more powerful for the next battle.
A dark and tragic world
The Kungfupunk aesthetic informs not only how Phantom Blade Zero looks, but also the stories you find within it — it’s a dark place, constantly steeped in tragedy. Those stories lead to epic, varied boss fights against powerful martial artists and corrupted, monstrous characters.
Hua, Deadly Betrothed, is an early optional boss who forces you to stay aware of your surroundings as she summons deadly spider lilies that sap your strength and stagger you, leaving you open to massive blows from her huge sword. Once you defeat her, you learn about how she was used by the man she was to marry, and her rage resulted in the massacre of the entire wedding party.
Verify your age to view this content.
Verify your age to view this content.
Other characters represent the powers hunting Soul throughout the game, whose motivations are slowly uncovered through flashbacks as you push forward. Jing Ye, The Outlaw, comes at you on horseback and employs dirty tricks, throwing dirt in your face to obscure your vision as he tries to run you down. When you finally knock him off his mount, he comes at you with a spiked shield that damages you when you attack, and a huge sword he’ll try to bury in your flesh to absorb your blood and heal himself.
Verify your age to view this content.
Verify your age to view this content.
And then there are characters with their own agendas, like the Gold-Masked One, a man you encounter in the strange illusory realm of the Discordance, played by actor and martial arts legend Donnie Yen. As you learn more about his shadowed story, he challenges you to vicious duels, using sword slashes, kicks, punches, and powerful, unblockable throws to rip through your life meter.
Developer S-Game’s attention to detail in each boss gives you a glimpse into their backstories, even as you fight them. Those tidbits help flesh out its world as much as the side quests and characters you’ll help along the way. Through these tragic stories, you quickly discover that the world of Phantom Blade Zero is harsh; not everyone you face in battle is evil, and you won’t be able to help everyone who needs you.
But at least you can take down the frightening monsters tormenting the innocent, one furious, beautiful battle at a time. Test your skills against the foes of the Wulin when Phantom Blade Zero hits PlayStation 5 on October 29.

items.title: Modern Warfare 4 Season 1: Everything you need to know for November 6 launch
items.content:
Get ready for Season 1, with new maps, modes, events and rewards across Multiplayer and DMZ. Explore the unforgiving corridors of X01, wield new weapons and attachments, acquire new Operator Skins, Weapon Blueprints, DMZ Survival Kits, and more. Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Season 1 goes live on November 6
Play Video
New Multiplayer maps and modes
Take the fight in Multiplayer across three new maps at Season 1 launch. Brave inclement weather across the all-new war torn Backstab, where abandoned tanks litter the landscape and drone ordinance line the shelves of a deserted dwelling. Battle amidst towering rock walls in the all-new Canyon and try your luck along the River near the Convoy Ambush or take the Cliff Path for its winding pathways. Drop into a reimagined Shoot House against the rugged terrain of North Korea during a snowfall.
Also, at Season 1 launch, play the fan-favorite Grind mode where you eliminate players, recover their dog tags, and take them to the Bank to score for your team. Plus, Drop Zone mode returns where teams fight to hold a single rotating objective with periodic Killstreak packages airdrop over the Drop Zone.
In the Mid-Season, we drop additional new maps and modes. Battle erupts at the all-new Ministry, causing damage to an embassy as you fight in and around the building on this diplomatic summit.
Overflow is the new map centered around a factory and its surrounding farmland. Counter Attack is a new mode where your focus is detonating bombs at the enemy Comm Station while protecting your own from attack.
DMZ’s new X01 weapon facility
A formerly undiscovered weapons facility —codenamed X01 — has recently been seized by enemy forces. X01’s maze of tunnels and shifting hazards calls for careful planning, specialized equipment, and squad coordination. Expect new and powerful equipment and as the facility starts to close off extraction points, complete the required steps to escape, or else! In addition, expect multiple pages of new DMZ Orders inside X01 with plenty to uncover on deployment along, Threat Briefing to take down DMZ’s biggest Boss threats from Commanders and more, and Resupply Runs.
New Warzone maps
Play across two new maps in Call of Duty: Warzone as the Season 1 update brings both Hajin and Zodiac with additional game modes, gameplay features, and more. More intel to arrive soon, including full roadmap covering everything coming to Call of Duty: Warzone in Season 1.
General content updates
Expand your arsenal of weapons with the arrival of the Cronen Osprey Assault Rifle and the CSG-35 SMG in the Season 1 Battle Pass. The Cronen Osprey combines speed with moderate power for an Assault Rifle that’s quick and reliable on the frontlines. The CSG-35 SMG excels at putting down enemies fast at close ranges as it features the highest fire rate in its class
The Season 1 Battle Pass is packed with 100+ pieces of unlockable content with an all-new catch-up system that guarantees 50+ rewards for those who purchase it. In addition to the normal unlocking of Battle Pass content, players who fall behind in the premium Battle Pass will be automatically caught up to the Reward matching the current day of the season, up to day 50. In addition, the Battle Pass itself is simpler to navigate, too: Log in to collect your rewards and keep playing to unlock a linear 100-tier track filled with additional Operator Skins, Weapon Blueprints, Finishing Moves, and more.

items.title: Thin, Light and Built for Everything: NVIDIA RTX Spark Windows Laptops Gain New Models, Agent Tools and Games
items.content:
NVIDIA RTX Spark powers thin and light laptops built for everything that developers, creators and gamers do.
RTX Spark laptops are now available from ASUS, Dell, HP, Lenovo, Microsoft and MSI. These powerful systems combine an NVIDIA Blackwell RTX GPU and an NVIDIA Grace CPU in a single superchip with up to 128GB of unified memory and up to 1 petaflop of FP4 AI performance. That puts the NVIDIA CUDA platform, RTX graphics and the capabilities of a personal AI supercomputer inside premium Windows laptops built to go anywhere.
New and expected RTX Spark updates, coming soon, include:
NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe, an open weight speech model for transcription, speaker attribution and translation is available on RTX Spark.
The LFM3 family of open models with day-zero support.
Resource management controls in NVIDIA App to allocate GPU resources between foreground apps and background agents.
Phantom Blade Zero, S-GAME’s highly-anticipated action role-playing game, launches with ray tracing and NVIDIA DLSS 4.5.
Experience Minecraft with path tracing and DLSS with RTX Remix1.6, available now for RTX Spark.
Turn Recorded Audio Into Useful Information With NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe
Introduced today, NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe is a new, open weight speech model that turns recorded conversations into useful information. Instead of needing multiple models for transcription, speaker labels and translation, developers can use one promptable model that handles all three, plus questions about the audio. It transcribes 40 languages, including seven Indic languages.
Developers guide the model with plain-language prompts. For example, for a single recorded meeting, users can ask it to:
“Transcribe this recording and label each speaker.”
“Translate this audio into English.”
“List what decisions were made in this meeting.”
Prompts can also include product terms and formatting conventions, which helps the model handle specialized vocabulary in fields like healthcare, financial services and customer service. Because the weights are open, developers can choose where audio is processed, from a desktop to the cloud.
Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe ranks No. 1 on the Hugging Face Open ASR and No. 2 among open weight models on Artificial Analysis — delivering leading accuracy with approximately 4.3 billion active parameters, 80% fewer than the No. 1 open weight model, making high-quality, intelligent transcription more practical on local hardware.
It’s available today on Hugging Face. Quantized versions are coming soon, so developers can run Transcribe locally onNVIDIA RTX Spark and DGX Spark systems, Jetson AGX Thor devices or scale up on NVIDIA Blackwell data center GPUs. NVFP4 versions will be deployable through NeMo-Speech.cpp or vLLM.
Learn more in the NVIDIA technical blog.
Control How Agents and PC Apps Share GPU Resources
On RTX Spark, users can have long-running agents working alongside their favorite applications. Both share the system’s GPU compute, and the right balance of resources depends on what matters to users at that moment.
With the new resource management feature in NVIDIA App, users can now choose how GPU resources are shared. They can prioritize their foreground app for the best performance, or give their background-running agent more resources to get work done faster.
Access control resource sharing from System > Advanced in the NVIDIA App. This feature requires hardware-accelerated GPU scheduling to be enabled in Windows Settings.
Liquid AI: One Model Family, Many Ways to Work
Liquid AI’s LFM3 provides a new generation of Liquid Foundation Models designed for specialized tasks. The family spans text, vision, audio, omni and decision models built on one shared backbone, with base and post-trained models available as open weights. The models are compact and fast: Liquid AI’s new 1.7-billion-parameter base model outperforms its previous 2.6-billion-parameter base model.
These models support local workflows such as agents running in Hermes Agent, Pi and OpenClaw to triage inboxes and manage calendars, read documents and app screens, transcribe and translate speech, answer spoken questions about handwritten math, and route support tickets or voice requests.
Developers can run LFM3 models on RTX Spark with native support through llama.cpp and vLLM, and fine-tune the models locally.
‘Phantom Blade Zero’ Launches With DLSS 4.5
S-GAME’s Phantom Blade Zero launches tonight, Oct. 28, at 7 p.m. PT on Steam and the Epic Games Store. Players can take on the role of Soul, a swordsman framed for his master’s murder, as he travels the martial world to uncover a conspiracy.
NVIDIA worked with S-GAME Studio and S-GAME Publishing to add ray-traced effects to the title. On RTX Spark laptops and GeForce RTX GPU-powered PCs, ray tracing adds more accurate bounced lighting, detailed reflections and realistic shadows on foliage and terrain. The NVIDIA DLSS Dynamic Multi Frame Generation feature boosts frame rates with up to 6x frame generation, or adjusts the multiplier on the fly to hit a player’s target frame rate.
Read more on GeForce.com.
RTX Remix Breathes New Life Into Classics
NVIDIA RTX Remix, the modding platform for remastering classic games with path tracing and DLSS, released version 1.6 last week. This update brought RTX Remix to the world’s largest gaming community: Minecraft. Both creators and players can render Minecraft Java Edition 1.21.1 through RTX Remix with DLSS-accelerated path tracing and take full advantage of realistic lighting and materials in their future creations.
The update also adds DLSS 5 with 3D-Guided Neural Rendering, up to 6x Multi Frame Generation, native RTX Spark support and agent-assisted workflows. Starting today, those upgrades come to Portal with RTX and the Half-Life 2 RTX demo. Both now support RTX Spark, with DLSS 3D-Guided Neural Rendering for more lifelike lighting and materials, a new Performance Mode for DLSS Frame Generation and new options that speed up path tracing.
RTX Remix 1.6 also makes AI-powered modding simpler. A redesigned ComfyUI workflow lets modders generate physically based materials directly inside RTX Remix, with no application programming interface setup, batch processing for full projects and presets for less technical creators. Plus, with NVIDIA agent skills, compatible AI agents can work directly with RTX Remix to help speed up remastering projects.
Learn more in the RTX Remix blog.
RTX Spark Laptops: Beautifully Designed, Built for Everything
RTX Spark laptops come in a range of designs, so users can choose one that fits how they work and play. Options include different screen sizes, colors, touchscreens, pen support and two-in-one convertibles. RTX Spark laptops are as thin as 14mm and as light as three pounds, with all-day battery life.
Such slim designs are possible because RTX Spark places the GPU, CPU and up to 128GB of unified memory on one power-efficient superchip. Creative projects and AI models draw from the same memory pool, so a laptop can take on work that used to call for a desktop workstation, even when unplugged.
Here’s what this means for:
AI developers: Run models and agents locally on NVIDIA CUDA — the same platform that powers AI in the cloud — with a path to deploy across more than 150 million NVIDIA RTX AI PCs and NVIDIA GPUs in the cloud.
Creators: RTX Spark can edit camera native 4:2:2 video and render 3D scenes of up to 90GB. Adobe Photoshop and Premiere offer native RTX Spark support through beta releases.
Gamers: Hundreds of games run on RTX Spark, with NVIDIA DLSS, ray tracing, Reflex and G-SYNC delivering sharper visuals and smoother, more responsive gameplay.
RTX Spark laptops are available now from ASUS, Dell, HP, Lenovo, Microsoft and MSI, starting at $2,599, with 128GB configurations on shelves. Find a laptop on the RTX Spark product page.
#ICYMI: More Updates From NVIDIA Local AI
Microducks learn to walk with help from RTX Spark: During the GTC Berlin keynote, NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang showed how AI agents running on RTX Spark can help train Hugging Face’s Microduck robot. A new NVIDIA technical blog walks through the workflow: Hermes Agent and Nemotron 3.5 Bolt plan an obstacle course on RTX Spark, Astra builds the 3D assets, NVIDIA Isaac Lab trains the navigation policy and RTX Spark validates it in NVIDIA Isaac Sim. Watch the demo and try the playbook.
NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB is now available, enabling natural conversations and multistep agent tasks with as little as 4GB of memory. The model powers local voice assistants, game characters and embedded interfaces on RTX Spark, DGX Spark, GeForce RTX GPUs and NVIDIA Jetson devices. It supports llama.cpp, vLLM, Ollama, Unsloth and LM Studio, and works with Hermes and OpenClaw. For more demanding agent workloads, Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB is designed to run local agents on RTX Spark.
Black Forest Labs’ FLUX 3 Image Klein is a 5.6-billion-parameter open weights model that lets users generate and edit images locally. NVIDIA-optimized versions run on RTX GPUs with as little as 8GB of VRAM. Developers can also fine-tune the model on RTX Spark using an NVIDIA NeMo AutoModel recipe to customize it for specific creative workflows.
NVIDIA DGX Spark 64GB is now available to purchase from manufacturer partners, giving developers and researchers another way to build and run AI locally. Powered by the GB10 Grace Blackwell Superchip, it combines 64GB of unified memory with DGX OS and the NVIDIA AI software stack for agent development, inference and fine-tuning. Learn more and explore purchase options.
Follow NVIDIA RTX Spark on X, Instagram, TikTok and Facebook — and stay informed by subscribing to the NVIDIA Local AI newsletter. Follow NVIDIA Workstation on LinkedIn and X.
